.cfm-sb-art-wrap {

.cfm-sb-art-eq span:nth-child(2) { height: 38px; }
.cfm-sb-art-eq span:nth-child(3) { height: 26px; }
.cfm-sb-art-eq span:nth-child(4) { height: 48px; }
.cfm-sb-art-eq span:nth-child(5) { height: 32px; }
.cfm-sb-art-eq span:nth-child(6) { height: 44px; }
.cfm-sb-art-eq span:nth-child(7) { height: 24px; }

.cfm-sb-art.playing .cfm-sb-art-eq span:nth-child(1) { animation: cfm-sb-eq 1.1s ease-in-out infinite; }
.cfm-sb-art.playing .cfm-sb-art-eq span:nth-child(2) { animation: cfm-sb-eq 0.9s ease-in-out infinite 0.1s; }
.cfm-sb-art.playing .cfm-sb-art-eq span:nth-child(3) { animation: cfm-sb-eq 1.2s ease-in-out infinite 0.16s; }

.cfm-sb-art.playing .cfm-sb-art-eq span:nth-child(5) { animation: cfm-sb-eq 1.15s ease-in-out infinite 0.18s; }
.cfm-sb-art.playing .cfm-sb-art-eq span:nth-child(6) { animation: cfm-sb-eq 0.96s ease-in-out infinite 0.14s; }
.cfm-sb-art.playing .cfm-sb-art-eq span:nth-child(7) { animation: cfm-sb-eq 1.18s ease-in-out infinite 0.06s; }
.cfm-sb-art.playing .cfm-sb-art-eq span:nth-child(8) { animation: cfm-sb-eq 1.02s ease-in-out infinite 0.12s; }
.cfm-sb-art.playing .cfm-sb-art-ring { animation: cfm-sb-spin 7s linear infinite; }
.cfm-sb-art.playing .cfm-sb-art-ring.cfm-sb-art-ring-b { animation-duration: 4.4s; animation-direction: reverse; }
.cfm-sb-art.playing .cfm-sb-art-orbital.cfm-sb-orbital-a { animation: cfm-sb-orbit-a 6s linear infinite; }
.cfm-sb-art.playing .cfm-sb-art-orbital.cfm-sb-orbital-b { animation: cfm-sb-orbit-b 7.4s linear infinite reverse; }
@keyframes cfm-sb-glow { 0%,100% { box-shadow: inset 0 0 40px rgba(74,158,255,0.07); } 50% { box-shadow: inset 0 0 80px rgba(74,158,255,0.14); } }
@keyframes cfm-sb-eq { 0%,100% { transform: scaleY(0.6); } 50% { transform: scaleY(1.12); } }
@keyframes cfm-sb-spin { from { transform: rotate(0deg); } to { transform: rotate(360deg); } }
@keyframes cfm-sb-orbit-a {
  0%   { transform: translate(0, 0); }
  25%  { transform: translate(14px, 8px); }
  50%  { transform: translate(32px, 26px); }
  75%  { transform: translate(10px, 46px); }
  100% { transform: translate(0, 0); }
}
@keyframes cfm-sb-orbit-b {
  0%   { transform: translate(0, 0); }
  25%  { transform: translate(-12px, -8px); }
  50%  { transform: translate(-28px, -22px); }
  75%  { transform: translate(-8px, -42px); }
  100% { transform: translate(0, 0); }
}
@media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce) {
  .cfm-sb-art.playing,
  .cfm-sb-art.playing .cfm-sb-art-eq span,
  .cfm-sb-art.playing .cfm-sb-art-ring,
  .cfm-sb-art.playing .cfm-sb-art-orbital {
    animation: none !important;
  }
}

      <div class="announce-item"><span class="announce-date">Jul 20, 2026</span><span class="announce-badge badge-new">New</span><div class="announce-text"><strong>KTHQ songs are now on streaming.</strong> The ContractingFM catalog is out as the <em>KTHQ Soundtrack</em> album on <a href="https://open.spotify.com/artist/7oNrK1I1AKGpqlHLNyDdtk" target="_blank" rel="noopener">Spotify</a>, Apple Music, Amazon Music, YouTube Music, and the other major services, so you can stream it on your commute, at the gym, or anywhere outside the site.         <summary style="cursor:pointer;color:#4a9eff;font-size:0.88rem;font-weight:600;padding:0.5rem 0;">Older announcements</summary>
        <div style="margin-top:0.5rem;display:flex;flex-direction:column;gap:0.45rem;">
          <div class="announce-item"><span class="announce-date">Jul 10, 2026</span><span class="announce-badge badge-new">New</span><div class="announce-text"><strong>Country research dossier and full-site QC.</strong> The new <a href="country-contracting-dossier.html">Country Contracting Dossier</a> is live in <a href="tools.html">Tools</a>, bringing open-source country research, vendor discovery, clearance references, finance data, and CCO briefing support into one working view. We also completed an overall quality-control review of the site and fact-checked contracting content against current Revolutionary FAR Overhaul materials and official sources. As always, please let us know if you have any feedback!</div></div>
          <div class="announce-item"><span class="announce-date">Jun 3, 2026</span><span class="announce-badge badge-new">New</span><div class="announce-text"><strong>AI lives in the PWS Builder.</strong> The <a href="pws-builder.html">PWS Builder</a> now has Draft with AI buttons on every section. Each one builds a prompt from what you've already filled in and uses Google's Gemini to draft the next piece, with a built-in rule against inventing FAR section numbers and an explicit reminder to verify any regulatory references against the Revolutionary FAR Overhaul before publishing. Every Gemini call costs a few cents on the back end. If it saves you time, <a href="https://www.buymeacoffee.com/nhazelett" target="_blank" rel="noopener">buying me a coffee</a> keeps the lights on and helps fund more AI features across the site.</div></div>
          <div class="announce-item"><span class="announce-date">May 20, 2026</span><span class="announce-badge badge-update">Update</span><div class="announce-text"><strong>A big day for CCOs.</strong> New and rewritten contingency contracting modules went live: OCS for Dummies Part 2 (BOS, the JRRB no-shit rundown, Annex W products, SPOT/JAMMS, the handoff card), Establishing DoDAACs, Purchasing Food and Water in a Contingency, SF 44 Purchases, MIPRs in a Deployed Environment, and a full rewrite of the Field Ordering Officer Program. AFCAP framing was tightened across the contingency hub. Start at the <a href="contingency-contracting.html">Contingency Contracting Field Desk</a> and work outward. Cleanup: 10 new songs on ContractingFM, a few small bugs squashed, and a tighter quality filter on RFO vs legacy FAR citations. The site has always tried to flag when content pulls specifically from the Revolutionary FAR Overhaul, but you'll now see more explicit clarification when training is RFO-sourced versus legacy FAR. Old guidance should not sneak through. A note on cadence: expect fewer announcements going forward as we lean into quality of content over quantity of releases. Rest assured, I am still obsessed with bringing you updates.</div></div>
          <div class="announce-item"><span class="announce-date">May 10, 2026</span><span class="announce-badge badge-new">New</span><div class="announce-text"><strong>KTHQ Community is live.</strong> I added a <a href="https://forum.kthq.org" target="_blank" rel="noopener">forum for contracting questions</a>, tool support, warrant prep, FAR/DFARS discussion, PWS help, COR topics, and feature requests. Keep examples sanitized: no CUI, PII, source-selection information, contractor proprietary information, or live acquisition details.</div></div>

<script>
  (function () {
    var MONTHS = { Jan: 0, Feb: 1, Mar: 2, Apr: 3, May: 4, Jun: 5, Jul: 6, Aug: 7, Sep: 8, Oct: 9, Nov: 10, Dec: 11 };

    function parsePublicationDate(text) {
      var match = /^([A-Z][a-z]{2})\s+(\d{1,2}),\s+(\d{4})$/.exec((text || '').trim());
      if (!match || MONTHS[match[1]] === undefined) return null;
      var year = Number(match[3]);
      var month = MONTHS[match[1]];
      var day = Number(match[2]);
      var date = new Date(Date.UTC(year, month, day, 12));
      if (date.getUTCFullYear() !== year || date.getUTCMonth() !== month || date.getUTCDate() !== day) return null;
      return {
        sortValue: date.getTime(),
        dateKey: year + '-' + String(month + 1).padStart(2, '0') + '-' + String(day).padStart(2, '0'),
        display: match[1] + ' ' + day + ', ' + year
      };
    }

    function easternDateKey(value) {
      var parts = new Intl.DateTimeFormat('en-US', {
        timeZone: 'America/New_York',
        year: 'numeric',
        month: '2-digit',
        day: '2-digit'
      }).formatToParts(value);
      var byType = {};
      parts.forEach(function (part) { byType[part.type] = part.value; });
      return byType.year + '-' + byType.month + '-' + byType.day;
    }

    function collectBriefs(root) {
      return Array.prototype.map.call(root.querySelectorAll('.announce-list .announce-item'), function (item) {
        var dateElement = item.querySelector('.announce-date');
        var content = item.querySelector('.announce-text');
        var parsed = parsePublicationDate(dateElement && dateElement.textContent);
        if (!parsed || !content) return null;
        var sourceLink = content.querySelector('a[href]');
        var titleElement = content.querySelector('strong');
        return {
          sortValue: parsed.sortValue,
          dateKey: parsed.dateKey,
          display: parsed.display,
          kicker: (item.querySelector('.announce-badge') || {}).textContent || 'Update',
          title: (titleElement ? titleElement.textContent : content.textContent).trim(),
          href: sourceLink ? sourceLink.getAttribute('href') : '#welcome',
          target: sourceLink ? sourceLink.getAttribute('target') : '',
          rel: sourceLink ? sourceLink.getAttribute('rel') : ''
        };
      }).filter(Boolean).sort(function (a, b) { return b.sortValue - a.sortValue; });
    }

    function renderLatestBrief(options) {
      options = options || {};
      var root = options.root || document;
      var briefs = options.items || collectBriefs(root);
      var latest = briefs[0];
      if (!latest) return null;

      var label = root.getElementById('homeLatestBriefLabel');
      var date = root.getElementById('homeLatestBriefDate');
      var link = root.getElementById('homeLatestBriefLink');
      var kicker = root.getElementById('homeLatestBriefKicker');
      var title = root.getElementById('homeLatestBriefTitle');
      var card = root.getElementById('homeLatestBrief');
      if (!label || !date || !link || !kicker || !title || !card) return null;

      label.textContent = latest.dateKey === easternDateKey(options.now || new Date()) ? 'Today’s Brief' : 'Latest Brief';
      date.dateTime = latest.dateKey;
      date.textContent = latest.display;
      link.setAttribute('href', latest.href || '#welcome');
      if (latest.target) link.setAttribute('target', latest.target); else link.removeAttribute('target');
      if (latest.rel) link.setAttribute('rel', latest.rel); else link.removeAttribute('rel');
      kicker.textContent = (latest.kicker || 'Update').trim();
      title.textContent = latest.title;
      card.setAttribute('data-brief-state', 'automatic');
      return latest;
    }

    window.KTHQBrief = {
      parsePublicationDate: parsePublicationDate,
      easternDateKey: easternDateKey,
      collectBriefs: collectBriefs,
      renderLatestBrief: renderLatestBrief
    };

    try { renderLatestBrief(); } catch (error) { /* Keep the static fallback card intact. */ }
  })();
</script>

<!DOCTYPE html><html lang="en" style="--cfm-accent: #ef4444;"><head>
  <!-- Google tag (gtag.js) -->
  <script async="" src="https://www.googletagmanager.com/gtag/js?id=G-X2RXS78N7K"></script>
  <script>window.dataLayer=window.dataLayer||[];function gtag(){dataLayer.push(arguments);}gtag("js",new Date());gtag("config","G-X2RXS78N7K");</script>
  <meta charset="UTF-8">
  <meta name="viewport" content="width=device-width, initial-scale=1.0">
  <meta name="description" content="Learn how Statements of Objectives work in federal contracting. Interactive SOO examples for new contracting officers.">
  <title>Statements of Objectives | ContractingHQ</title>
  <link rel="preconnect" href="https://fonts.googleapis.com">
  <link rel="preconnect" href="https://fonts.gstatic.com" crossorigin="">
  <link href="https://fonts.googleapis.com/css2?family=Inter:wght@300;400;500;600;700;800&family=Rajdhani:wght@500;600;700&display=swap" rel="stylesheet">
  <link rel="stylesheet" href="styles.css">
  <style>
    .soo-bg { background: #040d1f; padding: 0 0 6rem; min-height: 80vh; }

    .soo-tabs { display: flex; gap: 0; border-bottom: 1px solid rgba(74,158,255,0.15); background: rgba(4,13,31,0.95); position: sticky; top: 0; z-index: 90; backdrop-filter: blur(8px); flex-wrap: wrap; }
    .soo-tab { padding: 0.85rem 1.5rem; font-size: 0.85rem; font-weight: 700; text-transform: uppercase; letter-spacing: 1px; color: var(--silver); background: none; border: none; border-bottom: 3px solid transparent; cursor: pointer; transition: all 0.18s; font-family: inherit; white-space: nowrap; }
    .soo-tab:hover { color: var(--white); }
    .soo-tab.active { color: var(--accent); border-bottom-color: var(--accent); }
    .soo-panel { display: none; padding: 3rem 1.5rem; max-width: 900px; margin: 0 auto; }
    .soo-panel.active { display: block; }

    .soo-intro { text-align: center; padding: 2.5rem 1.5rem 0; }
    .soo-intro-tag { display: inline-block; background: rgba(74,158,255,0.1); border: 1px solid rgba(74,158,255,0.25); color: var(--accent); font-size: 0.68rem; font-weight: 700; letter-spacing: 2px; text-transform: uppercase; padding: 0.25rem 0.9rem; border-radius: 100px; margin-bottom: 0.65rem; }
    .soo-intro h2 { font-family: 'Rajdhani', sans-serif; font-size: clamp(1.4rem,3vw,2rem); font-weight: 700; color: var(--white); margin-bottom: 0.4rem; }
    .soo-intro p { color: var(--silver); font-size: 0.9rem; max-width: 620px; margin: 0 auto 1.5rem; line-height: 1.6; }

    .learn-section { margin-bottom: 2.5rem; }
    .learn-section h3 { font-family: 'Rajdhani', sans-serif; font-size: 1.35rem; font-weight: 700; color: var(--white); margin-bottom: 0.75rem; display: flex; align-items: center; gap: 0.5rem; }
    .learn-section h3 .section-num { display: inline-flex; align-items: center; justify-content: center; width: 30px; height: 30px; border-radius: 8px; background: rgba(74,158,255,0.12); color: var(--accent); font-size: 0.85rem; font-weight: 700; flex-shrink: 0; }
    .learn-body { color: var(--silver); font-size: 0.92rem; line-height: 1.75; }
    .learn-body p { margin-bottom: 1rem; }
    .learn-body strong { color: var(--white); font-weight: 600; }
    .learn-body .highlight-box { background: rgba(74,158,255,0.05); border: 1px solid rgba(74,158,255,0.15); border-radius: 12px; padding: 1rem 1.25rem; margin: 1rem 0; font-size: 0.88rem; }
    .learn-body .highlight-box.warn { background: rgba(248,113,113,0.05); border-color: rgba(248,113,113,0.2); }
    .learn-body .highlight-box.warn strong { color: #fca5a5; }
    .learn-body .highlight-box.tip { background: rgba(52,211,153,0.05); border-color: rgba(52,211,153,0.2); }
    .learn-body .highlight-box.tip strong { color: #6ee7b7; }
    .learn-divider { border: none; border-top: 1px solid rgba(74,158,255,0.08); margin: 2rem 0; }

    .soo-outer { background: rgba(10,22,50,0.3); border-radius: 14px; padding: 1.5rem; overflow-x: auto; }
    .soo-doc { min-width: 650px; border: 2px solid #000; background: #fff; color: #000; font-size: 12px; line-height: 1.6; font-family: 'Inter', 'Times New Roman', serif; padding: 2rem 2.5rem; }
    .soo-doc h4 { font-size: 14px; font-weight: 700; text-transform: uppercase; text-align: center; margin-bottom: 1.5rem; letter-spacing: 1px; border-bottom: 2px solid #000; padding-bottom: 0.5rem; }
    .soo-doc h5 { font-size: 12px; font-weight: 700; margin: 1.25rem 0 0.5rem; text-transform: uppercase; }

    .soo-section { padding: 0.6rem 0.75rem; margin: 0.5rem 0; border-radius: 4px; cursor: pointer; transition: background 0.12s; border-left: 3px solid transparent; }
    .soo-section:hover { background: #f0f4ff; }
    .soo-section.active { background: #fff9db; }
    .soo-section.soo-flag { border-left-color: #4a9eff; }
    .soo-section.soo-problem { border-left-color: #dc2626; }

    .soo-toggle { display: flex; gap: 0; margin-bottom: 1.25rem; }
    .soo-toggle-btn { flex: 1; padding: 0.75rem 1rem; font-size: 0.85rem; font-weight: 700; border: 1px solid rgba(74,158,255,0.2); background: rgba(10,22,50,0.5); color: var(--silver); cursor: pointer; transition: all 0.18s; font-family: inherit; }
    .soo-toggle-btn:first-child { border-radius: 8px 0 0 8px; }
    .soo-toggle-btn:last-child { border-radius: 0 8px 8px 0; }
    .soo-toggle-btn.active { background: rgba(74,158,255,0.15); color: var(--accent); border-color: rgba(74,158,255,0.4); }
    .soo-toggle-btn.bad.active { background: rgba(220,38,38,0.12); color: #fca5a5; border-color: rgba(220,38,38,0.35); }

    .soo-overlay { display: none; position: fixed; inset: 0; background: rgba(0,0,0,0.6); z-index: 200; align-items: center; justify-content: center; padding: 1.5rem; }
    .soo-overlay.visible { display: flex; }
    .soo-popup { background: #0d1a33; border: 1px solid rgba(74,158,255,0.3); border-radius: 14px; padding: 1.5rem 1.75rem; max-width: 520px; width: 100%; box-shadow: 0 8px 40px rgba(0,0,0,0.5); animation: popIn 0.18s ease-out; position: relative; }
    .soo-popup.warn { border-color: rgba(220,38,38,0.4); }
    .soo-popup-title { font-family: 'Rajdhani', sans-serif; font-size: 1.15rem; font-weight: 700; color: var(--accent); margin-bottom: 0.6rem; padding-right: 2rem; }
    .soo-popup.warn .soo-popup-title { color: #fca5a5; }
    .soo-popup-body { color: var(--silver); font-size: 0.9rem; line-height: 1.75; }
    .soo-popup-body strong { color: var(--white); }
    .soo-popup-close { position: absolute; top: 1rem; right: 1rem; background: none; border: none; color: var(--silver); cursor: pointer; font-size: 1.4rem; line-height: 1; padding: 0; transition: color 0.12s; }
    .soo-popup-close:hover { color: var(--white); }
    @keyframes popIn { from { opacity: 0; transform: scale(0.95); } to { opacity: 1; transform: scale(1); } }

    /* Flow diagram */
    .flow-diagram { display: flex; align-items: center; justify-content: center; gap: 0.5rem; flex-wrap: wrap; margin: 1.5rem 0; }
    .flow-step { background: rgba(10,22,50,0.7); border: 1px solid rgba(74,158,255,0.2); border-radius: 10px; padding: 0.75rem 1rem; text-align: center; min-width: 120px; }
    .flow-step-label { font-size: 0.68rem; color: var(--silver); text-transform: uppercase; letter-spacing: 0.5px; margin-bottom: 0.25rem; }
    .flow-step-text { font-size: 0.85rem; font-weight: 700; color: var(--white); }
    .flow-step.active-step { border-color: rgba(52,211,153,0.4); background: rgba(52,211,153,0.08); }
    .flow-step.active-step .flow-step-text { color: #6ee7b7; }
    .flow-step.fade-step { opacity: 0.5; }
    .flow-arrow { color: var(--accent); font-size: 1.2rem; flex-shrink: 0; }

    .lookup-grid { display: grid; grid-template-columns: repeat(auto-fit, minmax(280px, 1fr)); gap: 1.25rem; margin-top: 1.5rem; }
    .lookup-card { background: rgba(10,22,50,0.7); border: 1px solid rgba(74,158,255,0.12); border-radius: 14px; padding: 1.5rem; transition: all 0.2s; }
    .lookup-card:hover { border-color: rgba(74,158,255,0.3); transform: translateY(-2px); }
    .lookup-card h4 { font-family: 'Rajdhani', sans-serif; font-size: 1.1rem; font-weight: 700; color: var(--white); margin-bottom: 0.5rem; }
    .lookup-card p { color: var(--silver); font-size: 0.85rem; line-height: 1.6; margin-bottom: 1rem; }
    .lookup-card a { display: inline-flex; align-items: center; gap: 0.4rem; color: var(--accent); font-size: 0.85rem; font-weight: 700; text-decoration: none; transition: all 0.18s; }
    .lookup-card a:hover { color: var(--white); }
    .lookup-card a::after { content: '\2197'; font-size: 0.9rem; }

    @media (max-width: 768px) {
      .soo-tab { padding: 0.7rem 0.9rem; font-size: 0.75rem; }
      .soo-doc { padding: 1.25rem 1rem; min-width: auto; }
      .flow-diagram { gap: 0.35rem; }
      .flow-step { min-width: 90px; padding: 0.5rem 0.6rem; }
      .lookup-grid { grid-template-columns: 1fr; }
    }

  </style>

.cfm-playlist-count {
  display: inline-grid; place-items: center;
  min-width: 1.35rem; height: 1.35rem; padding: 0 0.28rem;

  color: #dbe8f7;
  font-size: 0.68rem; font-weight: 800;

.cfm-cco-toggle {
  position: relative;
  height: 100%;
  display: inline-flex;
  align-items: center;
  justify-content: center;

  border-left: 1px solid rgba(255,255,255,0.06);
  background: rgba(217,154,49,0.04);
  color: #8a9bb0;
  cursor: pointer;
  flex-shrink: 0;
  font-family: 'Inter', sans-serif;

.cfm-cco-toggle span {
  border: 1px solid rgba(217,154,49,0.28);

  font-size: 0.68rem;
  font-weight: 900;
  letter-spacing: 0.08em;

.cfm-cco-toggle:hover span,
.cfm-cco-toggle:focus-visible span,
.cfm-cco-toggle.active span {
  color: #080905;
  background: #d99a31;
  border-color: #d99a31;
}
.cfm-cco-toggle::after {
  content: attr(data-tip);
  position: absolute;
  right: 0.5rem;
  bottom: calc(100% + 10px);
  width: min(300px, calc(100vw - 24px));
  padding: 0.65rem 0.75rem;
  border: 1px solid rgba(217,154,49,0.34);
  border-radius: 8px;
  background: rgba(6,3,16,0.96);

  opacity: 0;
  pointer-events: none;
  transform: translateY(4px);
  transition: opacity 0.16s ease, transform 0.16s ease;
}
.cfm-cco-toggle:hover::after,
.cfm-cco-toggle:focus-visible::after {
  opacity: 1;
  transform: translateY(0);

.cfm-cco-toggle::after,
.cfm-sb-cco-toggle::after {
  content: none !important;

/* Playlist drawer */
#cfm-drawer {
  position: fixed; bottom: 68px; right: 0;

    <span class="hero-badge">Beginner Track • Topic 8</span>
    <h1 class="page-hero-title">Statements of Objectives</h1>
    <p class="page-hero-sub">A Statement of Objectives tells industry what you need to accomplish and asks them to propose how. It's the least prescriptive work statement, the least common in operational contracting, and the one that changes your entire solicitation strategy.</p>
  </div>

  <div class="soo-tabs" role="tablist">

  <!-- ═══════════════════════════════════ LEARN ═══ -->
  <div id="panel-learn" class="soo-panel active">
    <div class="soo-intro">
      <div class="soo-intro-tag">The Basics</div>
      <h2>What Is a Statement of Objectives?</h2>
      <p>You describe the problem. Industry proposes the solution. The winning contractor's proposed PWS becomes the contract's work statement.</p>
    </div>

    <div class="learn-section">
      <h3><span class="section-num">1</span> The SOO in Plain English</h3>
      <div class="learn-body">
        <p>A Statement of Objectives is the government saying: "Here's what we need to accomplish. We're not going to tell you how to do it, and we're not even going to define the performance standards. We want <em>you</em> to tell <em>us</em> how you'd solve this problem."</p>
        <p>Per <strong>FAR 37.602</strong>, offerors use the SOO to develop a Performance Work Statement. The offeror proposes the PWS as part of their proposal, and the winning PWS gets incorporated into the contract. The SOO itself does <strong>not</strong> become part of the contract. It stays in the source selection file.</p>
        <div class="highlight-box">
          <strong>The FAR requires the SOO to include, at a minimum:</strong><br><br>
          1. Purpose<br>
          2. Scope or mission<br>
          3. Period and place of performance<br>
          4. Background<br>
          5. Performance objectives (required results)<br>
          6. Any operating constraints
        </div>
        <p>That's it. No step-by-step procedures (that's a SOW). No measurable performance standards (that's a PWS). Just objectives and constraints. The contractor fills in everything else.</p>
      </div>
    </div>

    <hr class="learn-divider">

    <div class="learn-section">
      <h3><span class="section-num">2</span> How It Changes Your Solicitation</h3>
      <div class="learn-body">
        <p>Using an SOO doesn't just change the work statement. It changes everything downstream.</p>
        <div class="highlight-box warn">
          <strong>Evaluation factors must account for the proposed PWS.</strong> If you're asking offerors to propose their own approach, you have to evaluate those proposed approaches. That means your evaluation criteria need a factor for "quality of the proposed PWS" or "technical approach." You can't ask for a technical solution and then ignore it in evaluation.
        </div>
        <div class="highlight-box warn">
          <strong>This almost always means a tradeoff source selection.</strong> When every offeror is proposing a different PWS, the technical solutions won't be apples-to-apples. Lowest Price Technically Acceptable (LPTA) doesn't work well here because "technically acceptable" is hard to define when each proposal describes a different scope of work. You need evaluators who can assess the relative quality of different approaches and weigh them against price.
        </div>
        <div class="highlight-box">
          <strong>The practical implication:</strong> An SOO means more work for the source selection team, more complexity in the evaluation, and a longer timeline. That's not bad. It's just a tradeoff you need to plan for.
        </div>

        <!-- Flow diagram -->
        <p style="margin-top:1.5rem;">Here's the lifecycle:</p>
        <div class="flow-diagram">
          <div class="flow-step">
            <div class="flow-step-label">Government Writes</div>
            <div class="flow-step-text">SOO</div>
          </div>
          <div class="flow-arrow">→</div>
          <div class="flow-step">
            <div class="flow-step-label">Included In</div>
            <div class="flow-step-text">Solicitation</div>
          </div>
          <div class="flow-arrow">→</div>
          <div class="flow-step">
            <div class="flow-step-label">Offerors Propose</div>
            <div class="flow-step-text">PWS</div>
          </div>
          <div class="flow-arrow">→</div>
          <div class="flow-step active-step">
            <div class="flow-step-label">Government Evaluates</div>
            <div class="flow-step-text">Proposed PWSs</div>
          </div>
          <div class="flow-arrow">→</div>
          <div class="flow-step active-step">
            <div class="flow-step-label">Winning PWS</div>
            <div class="flow-step-text">Goes in Contract</div>
          </div>
        </div>
        <div style="text-align:center; margin-top:0.75rem;">
          <div class="flow-step fade-step" style="display:inline-block;">
            <div class="flow-step-label">The SOO</div>
            <div class="flow-step-text" style="color:var(--silver);">Stays in the File</div>
          </div>
        </div>
      </div>
    </div>

    <hr class="learn-divider">

    <div class="learn-section">
      <h3><span class="section-num">3</span> SOO vs. PWS vs. SOW</h3>
      <div class="learn-body">
        <p>Where does the SOO fit relative to the other two? Think of it as a spectrum of government control:</p>
        <div style="background:rgba(10,22,50,0.5); border:1px solid rgba(74,158,255,0.15); border-radius:12px; padding:1.5rem; margin:1.25rem 0;">
          <div style="display:grid; grid-template-columns:1fr 1fr 1fr; gap:1rem; text-align:center;">
            <div>
              <div style="font-weight:700; color:var(--accent); font-family:'Rajdhani',sans-serif; font-size:0.95rem; margin-bottom:0.4rem;">SOW</div>
              <div style="font-size:0.8rem; color:var(--silver); line-height:1.5;">Government writes the method.<br>Contractor executes.</div>
              <div style="margin-top:0.5rem; font-size:0.72rem; color:var(--accent); font-weight:600;">MOST CONTROL</div>
            </div>
            <div>
              <div style="font-weight:700; color:#6ee7b7; font-family:'Rajdhani',sans-serif; font-size:0.95rem; margin-bottom:0.4rem;">PWS</div>
              <div style="font-size:0.8rem; color:var(--silver); line-height:1.5;">Government writes the standards.<br>Contractor chooses the method.</div>
              <div style="margin-top:0.5rem; font-size:0.72rem; color:#6ee7b7; font-weight:600;">MODERATE CONTROL</div>
            </div>
            <div>
              <div style="font-weight:700; color:#fbbf24; font-family:'Rajdhani',sans-serif; font-size:0.95rem; margin-bottom:0.4rem;">SOO</div>
              <div style="font-size:0.8rem; color:var(--silver); line-height:1.5;">Government writes the objectives.<br>Contractor proposes everything.</div>
              <div style="margin-top:0.5rem; font-size:0.72rem; color:#fbbf24; font-weight:600;">LEAST CONTROL</div>
            </div>
          </div>
          <div style="margin-top:1rem; height:6px; border-radius:3px; background:linear-gradient(to right, rgba(74,158,255,0.4), rgba(52,211,153,0.4), rgba(251,191,36,0.4));"></div>
          <div style="display:flex; justify-content:space-between; font-size:0.7rem; color:var(--silver); margin-top:0.35rem;">
            <span>Government directs everything</span>
            <span>Contractor proposes everything</span>
          </div>
        </div>
        <p>As you move from SOW to SOO, risk shifts from the government to the contractor, but the government also gives up control over the approach. An SOO gives maximum flexibility to the contractor and maximum innovation potential, but it also means the government has to trust the evaluation process to select the right solution.</p>
      </div>
    </div>

    <hr class="learn-divider">

    <div class="learn-section">
      <h3><span class="section-num">4</span> When Would You Actually Use One?</h3>
      <div class="learn-body">
        <p>SOOs are rare in operational contracting for good reason. Most base-level requirements are well understood. You know what you need, and either you know the method (SOW) or you know the outcome (PWS). An SOO is for when you're not even sure about the best outcome to measure.</p>
        <div class="highlight-box tip">
          <strong>Complex IT modernization.</strong> "We need to modernize our network infrastructure across 6 buildings. We don't know what the right architecture looks like. Tell us what you'd propose." The government knows the problem but not the solution.
        </div>
        <div class="highlight-box tip">
          <strong>New capability development.</strong> "We need a training system for a new weapons platform. No existing system does this. Propose your approach." The government knows what it needs to accomplish but has no baseline to write standards against.
        </div>
        <div class="highlight-box tip">
          <strong>Broad organizational support.</strong> "We need to improve our supply chain efficiency. We've tried several approaches. Tell us what you'd do differently." The government has tried and wants fresh thinking from industry.
        </div>
        <div class="highlight-box">
          <strong>The common thread:</strong> The government doesn't know enough about the solution to write a PWS. If you can write measurable performance standards, you should. If you can't because the problem is too novel or too complex, an SOO might be the right tool.
        </div>
      </div>
    </div>

    <hr class="learn-divider">

    <div class="learn-section">
      <h3><span class="section-num">5</span> Common Pitfalls</h3>
      <div class="learn-body">
        <div class="highlight-box warn">
          <strong>Using an SOO when a PWS would work.</strong> Don't use an SOO just because writing a PWS is harder. If you understand the requirement well enough to define outcomes and measurable standards, write a PWS. An SOO adds complexity to your solicitation, your evaluation, and your timeline. Only use it when you genuinely need industry to help define the approach.
        </div>
        <div class="highlight-box warn">
          <strong>Writing a PWS and calling it an SOO.</strong> If your "SOO" includes measurable performance standards, specific deliverables with deadlines, and detailed technical requirements, it's not an SOO. It's a PWS. The label matters because it tells offerors what kind of proposal to write.
        </div>
        <div class="highlight-box warn">
          <strong>Not adjusting your evaluation factors.</strong> If you issue an SOO but your evaluation criteria only look at price and past performance, you've defeated the purpose. The whole point is that offerors are proposing different technical approaches. You need evaluation factors that assess the quality of those proposals.
        </div>
        <div class="highlight-box warn">
          <strong>Forgetting the SOO doesn't go in the contract.</strong> Per FAR 37.602(c), the SOO does not become part of the contract. The contractor's proposed PWS does. If you accidentally incorporate the SOO into the contract alongside the winning PWS, you may create ambiguity about which document governs.
        </div>
      </div>
    </div>
  </div>

  <div id="panel-examples" class="soo-panel">
    <div class="soo-intro">
      <div class="soo-intro-tag">Interactive Tool</div>
      <h2>SOO Examples</h2>
      <p>Same HVAC scenario, written as an SOO. Click highlighted sections for coaching notes. <span style="color:var(--accent); font-weight:600;">Blue borders</span> highlight good SOO technique. <span style="color:#dc2626; font-weight:600;">Red borders</span> flag problems.</p>
    </div>

    <div class="soo-toggle">
      <button class="soo-toggle-btn active" onclick="showExample('good')">✅ Well-Written SOO</button>
      <button class="soo-toggle-btn bad" onclick="showExample('bad')">❌ Poorly-Written SOO</button>
    </div>

    <!-- ═══════ GOOD SOO ═══════ -->
    <div id="example-good" class="soo-example">
      <div class="soo-outer">
        <div class="soo-doc">
          <h4>Statement of Objectives<br><span style="font-size:11px; font-weight:400; letter-spacing:0;">HVAC Sustainment Services, Building 1240, Wright-Patterson AFB</span></h4>

          <div class="soo-section soo-flag" data-note="good-purpose" onclick="showNote('good-purpose')">
            <h5>1.0 Purpose</h5>
            <p>The Government seeks contractor solutions to provide comprehensive HVAC sustainment for Building 1240 at Wright-Patterson Air Force Base, Ohio. This building houses approximately 200 personnel across four floors and requires reliable climate control year-round. The Government is interested in innovative approaches that maximize system reliability while minimizing lifecycle costs.</p>
          </div>

          <div class="soo-section soo-flag" data-note="good-scope" onclick="showNote('good-scope')">
            <h5>2.0 Scope / Mission</h5>
            <p>The scope encompasses all activities necessary to ensure the twelve (12) commercial HVAC units in Building 1240 provide reliable heating, ventilation, and air conditioning. This includes, but is not limited to, preventive maintenance, corrective maintenance, emergency response, and system performance monitoring. The contractor's proposed approach should address the full lifecycle of HVAC sustainment for the building.</p>
          </div>

          <div class="soo-section" data-note="good-period" onclick="showNote('good-period')">
            <h5>3.0 Period and Place of Performance</h5>
            <p>Base period of 12 months with two (2) 12-month option periods. All work shall be performed at Building 1240, Wright-Patterson AFB, OH 45433.</p>
          </div>

          <div class="soo-section soo-flag" data-note="good-background" onclick="showNote('good-background')">
            <h5>4.0 Background</h5>
            <p>Building 1240 was constructed in 2003 and houses administrative and operational functions for the 88th Air Base Wing. The current HVAC system consists of twelve Carrier WeatherMaker 48TC rooftop units installed in 2015. Over the past two fiscal years, the Government has experienced increasing maintenance costs and unplanned downtime, with availability dropping below 85% during peak summer and winter months. The current maintenance approach has been prescriptive (Government-directed preventive maintenance on a quarterly schedule), and the Government is interested in whether alternative approaches could improve reliability and reduce total cost of ownership.</p>
          </div>

          <div class="soo-section soo-flag" data-note="good-objectives" onclick="showNote('good-objectives')">
            <h5>5.0 Performance Objectives</h5>
            <p>The Government's objectives for this requirement are:</p>
            <p style="padding-left:1rem;">
              a) Reliable climate control for building occupants throughout the contract period.<br>
              b) Timely restoration of failed HVAC units to minimize impact on mission operations.<br>
              c) Cost-effective sustainment approach that reduces total lifecycle costs relative to the current maintenance model.<br>
              d) Proactive identification of HVAC components approaching end of life, with recommendations for replacement or upgrade.
            </p>
            <p>Offerors shall propose measurable performance standards for each objective as part of their proposed Performance Work Statement.</p>
          </div>

          <div class="soo-section soo-flag" data-note="good-constraints" onclick="showNote('good-constraints')">
            <h5>6.0 Operating Constraints</h5>
            <p>a) All refrigerant handling must comply with EPA Clean Air Act, Section 608.<br>
            b) Work inside the building during duty hours (0700-1700, Mon-Fri) must be coordinated with the Facility Manager to minimize disruption to occupants.<br>
            c) The contractor shall not modify, replace, or upgrade any HVAC equipment without prior written approval from the Contracting Officer.<br>
            d) All contractor personnel requiring unescorted access to the building must possess a valid Common Access Card (CAC) or visitor pass.</p>
          </div>

          <div style="margin-top:1rem; padding:0.5rem 0.75rem; font-size:9px; color:#999; border-top:1px solid #ccc; text-align:center;">
            TRAINING EXAMPLE | NOT AN OFFICIAL GOVERNMENT DOCUMENT
          </div>
        </div>
      </div>

      <div class="highlight-box tip" style="margin-top:1.25rem;">
        <strong>What happens next?</strong> Offerors read this SOO and each propose their own PWS with measurable standards, a maintenance approach, deliverables, and staffing. One offeror might propose a traditional quarterly PM schedule. Another might propose a predictive maintenance approach using IoT sensors. The evaluation team assesses which proposed PWS best meets the objectives. The winning PWS goes into the contract. This SOO stays in the file.
      </div>
    </div>

      <div class="soo-outer">
        <div class="soo-doc">
          <h4>Statement of Objectives<br><span style="font-size:11px; font-weight:400; letter-spacing:0;">HVAC Maintenance, Building 1240</span></h4>

          <div class="soo-section soo-problem" data-note="bad-purpose" onclick="showNote('bad-purpose')">
            <h5>1.0 Purpose</h5>
            <p>The Government needs HVAC maintenance for Building 1240.</p>
          </div>

          <div class="soo-section soo-problem" data-note="bad-reqs" onclick="showNote('bad-reqs')">
            <h5>2.0 Requirements</h5>
            <p><strong>2.1</strong> The contractor shall maintain 95% operational availability across all HVAC units, measured monthly.</p>
            <p><strong>2.2</strong> The contractor shall respond to emergency service calls within 4 hours during duty hours and 8 hours during non-duty hours.</p>
            <p><strong>2.3</strong> The contractor shall perform quarterly preventive maintenance on all units including filter replacement, coil cleaning, and refrigerant checks.</p>
            <p><strong>2.4</strong> The contractor shall submit monthly performance reports within 10 business days showing availability per unit, service calls, and corrective actions.</p>
          </div>

          <div class="soo-section soo-problem" data-note="bad-standards" onclick="showNote('bad-standards')">
            <h5>3.0 Performance Standards</h5>
            <p><strong>3.1</strong> No more than 1 unit below 95% availability in any month.</p>
            <p><strong>3.2</strong> No more than 2 late emergency responses per quarter.</p>
            <p><strong>3.3</strong> Customer satisfaction rating of 4.0 or higher on a 5.0 scale.</p>
          </div>

          <div class="soo-section soo-problem" data-note="bad-missing" onclick="showNote('bad-missing')">
            <h5>4.0 Period of Performance</h5>
            <p>Base period: 1 April 2026 through 31 March 2027, with two 12-month options.</p>
          </div>

          <div class="soo-section soo-problem" data-note="bad-clauses" onclick="showNote('bad-clauses')">
            <h5>5.0 Administration</h5>
            <p><strong>5.1</strong> The Government may terminate this contract for convenience by providing 30 days written notice.</p>
            <p><strong>5.2</strong> The contractor shall comply with all applicable federal, state, and local regulations.</p>
          </div>

          <div style="margin-top:1rem; padding:0.5rem 0.75rem; font-size:9px; color:#999; border-top:1px solid #ccc; text-align:center;">

function showNote(key) {
  const n = notes[key];
  if (!n) return;
  document.querySelectorAll('.soo-section').forEach(s => s.classList.remove('active'));
  document.querySelectorAll('[data-note="' + key + '"]').forEach(el => el.classList.add('active'));
  const popup = document.getElementById('notePopup');
  popup.classList.toggle('warn', !!n.warn);
  document.getElementById('noteTitle').textContent = n.title;
  document.getElementById('noteBody').innerHTML = n.body;
  document.getElementById('noteOverlay').classList.add('visible');
}

function hideNote() {
  document.getElementById('noteOverlay').classList.remove('visible');
  document.querySelectorAll('.soo-section').forEach(s => s.classList.remove('active'));
}

<style>.bmc-btn{display:inline-flex;align-items:center;gap:.4rem;background:#FFDD00;color:#000;border-radius:8px;padding:.45rem 1rem;font-weight:700;font-size:.83rem;text-decoration:none;transition:opacity .2s,transform .15s}.bmc-btn:hover{opacity:.88;transform:translateY(-1px)}</style>
  <style>
    /* ── Page shell ── */
    .mc-bg { background: #040d1f; padding: 0 0 6rem; min-height: 80vh; }

    /* ── Tab bar ── */
    .mc-tabs { display: flex; gap: 0; border-bottom: 1px solid rgba(74,158,255,0.15); background: rgba(4,13,31,0.95); position: sticky; top: 0; z-index: 90; backdrop-filter: blur(8px); flex-wrap: wrap; }
    .mc-tab { padding: 0.85rem 1.5rem; font-size: 0.85rem; font-weight: 700; text-transform: uppercase; letter-spacing: 1px; color: var(--silver); background: none; border: none; border-bottom: 3px solid transparent; cursor: pointer; transition: all 0.18s; font-family: inherit; white-space: nowrap; }
    .mc-tab:hover { color: var(--white); }
    .mc-tab.active { color: var(--accent); border-bottom-color: var(--accent); }
    .mc-panel { display: none; padding: 3rem 1.5rem; max-width: 900px; margin: 0 auto; }
    .mc-panel.active { display: block; }

    /* ── Intro ── */
    .mc-intro { text-align: center; padding: 2.5rem 1.5rem 0; }
    .mc-intro-tag { display: inline-block; background: rgba(74,158,255,0.1); border: 1px solid rgba(74,158,255,0.25); color: var(--accent); font-size: 0.68rem; font-weight: 700; letter-spacing: 2px; text-transform: uppercase; padding: 0.25rem 0.9rem; border-radius: 100px; margin-bottom: 0.65rem; }
    .mc-intro h2 { font-family: 'Rajdhani', sans-serif; font-size: clamp(1.4rem,3vw,2rem); font-weight: 700; color: var(--white); margin-bottom: 0.4rem; }
    .mc-intro p { color: var(--silver); font-size: 0.9rem; max-width: 660px; margin: 0 auto 1.5rem; line-height: 1.6; }

    /* ── Learn ── */
    .learn-section { margin-bottom: 2.5rem; }
    .learn-section h3 { font-family: 'Rajdhani', sans-serif; font-size: 1.35rem; font-weight: 700; color: var(--white); margin-bottom: 0.75rem; display: flex; align-items: center; gap: 0.5rem; }
    .learn-section h3 .section-num { display: inline-flex; align-items: center; justify-content: center; width: 30px; height: 30px; border-radius: 8px; background: rgba(74,158,255,0.12); color: var(--accent); font-size: 0.85rem; font-weight: 700; flex-shrink: 0; }
    .learn-body { color: var(--silver); font-size: 0.92rem; line-height: 1.75; }
    .learn-body p { margin-bottom: 1rem; }
    .learn-body strong { color: var(--white); font-weight: 600; }
    .learn-body .highlight-box { background: rgba(74,158,255,0.05); border: 1px solid rgba(74,158,255,0.15); border-radius: 12px; padding: 1rem 1.25rem; margin: 1rem 0; font-size: 0.88rem; }
    .learn-body .highlight-box.warn { background: rgba(248,113,113,0.05); border-color: rgba(248,113,113,0.2); }
    .learn-body .highlight-box.warn strong { color: #fca5a5; }
    .learn-body .highlight-box.tip { background: rgba(52,211,153,0.05); border-color: rgba(52,211,153,0.2); }
    .learn-body .highlight-box.tip strong { color: #6ee7b7; }
    .learn-divider { border: none; border-top: 1px solid rgba(74,158,255,0.08); margin: 2rem 0; }

    /* ── UCF table ── */
    .ucf-table { width: 100%; border-collapse: collapse; font-size: 0.84rem; margin: 1rem 0; }
    .ucf-table th { background: rgba(74,158,255,0.1); color: var(--accent); font-weight: 700; text-align: left; padding: 0.6rem 0.9rem; border-bottom: 1px solid rgba(74,158,255,0.2); font-size: 0.75rem; text-transform: uppercase; letter-spacing: 0.5px; }
    .ucf-table td { color: var(--silver); padding: 0.55rem 0.9rem; border-bottom: 1px solid rgba(74,158,255,0.06); vertical-align: top; }
    .ucf-table tr.used td { background: rgba(52,211,153,0.05); color: var(--white); }
    .ucf-table td strong { color: var(--white); }
    .ucf-use { display: inline-block; padding: 0.12rem 0.5rem; border-radius: 100px; font-size: 0.68rem; font-weight: 700; }
    .ucf-use.yes { background: rgba(52,211,153,0.15); color: #6ee7b7; border: 1px solid rgba(52,211,153,0.3); }
    .ucf-use.no { background: rgba(248,113,113,0.08); color: #fca5a5; border: 1px solid rgba(248,113,113,0.15); }
    .ucf-use.sometimes { background: rgba(251,191,36,0.1); color: #fcd34d; border: 1px solid rgba(251,191,36,0.2); }

    /* ── Mock 1449 form ── */
    .mock-outer { background: rgba(10,22,50,0.3); border-radius: 14px; padding: 1.5rem; overflow-x: auto; }
    .mock-form { min-width: 700px; border: 2px solid #000; background: #fff; color: #000; font-size: 10px; line-height: 1.4; font-family: 'Inter', Arial, sans-serif; }
    .mock-cell { border: 1px solid #000; padding: 4px 6px; }
    .mock-lbl { font-size: 7px; font-weight: 700; text-transform: uppercase; letter-spacing: 0.3px; color: #444; }
    .mock-val { font-size: 10px; color: #000; margin-top: 2px; }
    .mock-click { cursor: pointer; transition: background 0.12s; }
    .mock-click:hover { background: #f0f4ff; }
    .mock-click.active { background: #fff9db; }
    .mock-important { border-left: 3px solid #2563eb; }
    .mock-header { background: #e5e7eb; font-weight: 700; text-align: center; padding: 6px; font-size: 9px; text-transform: uppercase; letter-spacing: 0.5px; border: 1px solid #000; }
    .mock-cb { display: inline-flex; align-items: center; gap: 3px; font-size: 9px; margin: 1px 4px 1px 0; }
    .mock-box { width: 10px; height: 10px; border: 1px solid #333; display: inline-block; flex-shrink: 0; background: #fff; }
    .mock-box.checked { background: #1a1a1a; }

    /* ── Popup overlay ── */
    .mc-overlay { position: fixed; inset: 0; background: rgba(0,0,0,0.7); z-index: 200; display: flex; align-items: center; justify-content: center; opacity: 0; pointer-events: none; transition: opacity 0.2s; padding: 1rem; }
    .mc-overlay.visible { opacity: 1; pointer-events: auto; }
    .mc-popup { background: #0b1a34; border: 1px solid rgba(74,158,255,0.25); border-radius: 14px; max-width: 550px; width: 100%; padding: 1.75rem; position: relative; max-height: 80vh; overflow-y: auto; }
    .mc-popup h3 { font-family: 'Rajdhani', sans-serif; font-size: 1.2rem; font-weight: 700; color: var(--white); margin-bottom: 0.75rem; }
    .mc-popup p, .mc-popup div { color: var(--silver); font-size: 0.88rem; line-height: 1.7; }
    .mc-popup strong { color: var(--white); }
    .mc-popup-close { position: absolute; top: 0.75rem; right: 0.75rem; background: rgba(74,158,255,0.1); border: 1px solid rgba(74,158,255,0.2); border-radius: 8px; color: var(--accent); cursor: pointer; width: 28px; height: 28px; display: flex; align-items: center; justify-content: center; font-size: 1rem; font-weight: 700; }

    /* ── Section attachment grid ── */
    .section-grid { display: grid; grid-template-columns: repeat(auto-fill, minmax(180px, 1fr)); gap: 0.75rem; margin: 1rem 0; }
    .section-card { background: rgba(10,22,50,0.4); border: 1px solid rgba(74,158,255,0.15); border-radius: 10px; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; text-align: center; }
    .section-card .sec-letter { font-family: 'Rajdhani', sans-serif; font-size: 1.5rem; font-weight: 700; color: var(--accent); }
    .section-card .sec-name { color: var(--silver); font-size: 0.78rem; margin-top: 0.2rem; }
    .section-card.needed { border-color: rgba(52,211,153,0.35); }
    .section-card.needed .sec-letter { color: #6ee7b7; }
    .section-card.skip { opacity: 0.4; }

    /* ── Tool link cards ── */
    .tool-link-grid { display: grid; grid-template-columns: 1fr 1fr; gap: 1rem; margin: 1.5rem 0; }
    @media (max-width: 600px) { .tool-link-grid { grid-template-columns: 1fr; } }
    .tool-link-card { background: rgba(10,22,50,0.5); border: 1px solid rgba(74,158,255,0.2); border-radius: 14px; padding: 1.25rem; text-decoration: none; display: block; transition: border-color 0.15s, background 0.15s; }
    .tool-link-card:hover { border-color: var(--accent); background: rgba(74,158,255,0.05); }
    .tool-link-card h4 { font-family: 'Rajdhani', sans-serif; font-size: 1.1rem; font-weight: 700; color: var(--accent); margin-bottom: 0.35rem; }
    .tool-link-card p { color: var(--silver); font-size: 0.83rem; line-height: 1.55; margin: 0; }

    /* ── Look It Up ── */
    .lookup-grid { display: grid; grid-template-columns: repeat(auto-fill, minmax(240px, 1fr)); gap: 1rem; }
    .lookup-card { background: rgba(10,22,50,0.4); border: 1px solid rgba(74,158,255,0.12); border-radius: 12px; padding: 1.1rem 1.25rem; }
    .lookup-card h4 { font-family: 'Rajdhani', sans-serif; font-size: 1rem; font-weight: 700; color: var(--white); margin-bottom: 0.4rem; }
    .lookup-card p { color: var(--silver); font-size: 0.82rem; line-height: 1.55; margin-bottom: 0.75rem; }
    .lookup-card a { display: inline-block; font-size: 0.78rem; font-weight: 600; color: var(--accent); text-decoration: none; padding: 0.3rem 0.75rem; border: 1px solid rgba(74,158,255,0.25); border-radius: 6px; transition: all 0.15s; }
    .lookup-card a:hover { background: rgba(74,158,255,0.1); border-color: var(--accent); }
  </style>

.cfm-meta { flex: 1; min-width: 0; }

}
.cfm-meta-sub {

.cfm-controls {

}

.cfm-progress-zone {

}
.cfm-time { font-size: 0.68rem; color: #445; flex-shrink: 0; min-width: 32px; }

.cfm-bar-wrap { flex: 1; position: relative; height: 4px; cursor: pointer; }
.cfm-bar-bg {

}

.cfm-volume-zone {

}
.cfm-vol-icon { font-size: 0.75rem; color: #445; cursor: pointer; }
input[type=range].cfm-vol-slider {

}

.cfm-playlist-btn {
  background: none; border: none; cursor: pointer;

}

.cfm-playlist-btn.open { color: var(--cfm-accent, #4a9eff); }
.cfm-playlist-text { font-size: 0.72rem; font-weight: 700; }
.cfm-playlist-count {
  display: inline-grid; place-items: center;
  min-width: 1.35rem; height: 1.35rem; padding: 0 0.28rem;
  border-radius: 999px;
  background: rgba(255,255,255,0.08);
  color: #dbe8f7;
  font-size: 0.68rem; font-weight: 800;
}
.cfm-cco-toggle {
  position: relative;
  height: 100%;
  display: inline-flex;
  align-items: center;
  justify-content: center;
  padding: 0 0.85rem;

  border-left: 1px solid rgba(255,255,255,0.06);
  background: rgba(217,154,49,0.04);
  color: #8a9bb0;

  flex-shrink: 0;
  font-family: 'Inter', sans-serif;
}
.cfm-cco-toggle span {
  border: 1px solid rgba(217,154,49,0.28);

  padding: 0.22rem 0.52rem;

  font-weight: 900;
  letter-spacing: 0.08em;
}
.cfm-cco-toggle:hover span,
.cfm-cco-toggle:focus-visible span,
.cfm-cco-toggle.active span {
  color: #080905;

}
.cfm-cco-toggle::after {
  content: attr(data-tip);
  position: absolute;
  right: 0.5rem;
  bottom: calc(100% + 10px);
  width: min(300px, calc(100vw - 24px));
  padding: 0.65rem 0.75rem;
  border: 1px solid rgba(217,154,49,0.34);
  border-radius: 8px;
  background: rgba(6,3,16,0.96);
  color: #dbe8f7;
  box-shadow: 0 14px 34px rgba(0,0,0,0.42);
  font-size: 0.72rem;

  line-height: 1.45;
  opacity: 0;
  pointer-events: none;
  transform: translateY(4px);
  transition: opacity 0.16s ease, transform 0.16s ease;
}
.cfm-cco-toggle:hover::after,
.cfm-cco-toggle:focus-visible::after {
  opacity: 1;
  transform: translateY(0);
}
.cfm-cco-toggle::after,
.cfm-sb-cco-toggle::after {
  content: none !important;
  display: none !important;
}

/* Playlist drawer */
#cfm-drawer {
  position: fixed; bottom: 68px; right: 0;
  width: 380px; max-height: min(560px, calc(100vh - 92px));
  background: #080414;
  border: 1px solid rgba(255,255,255,0.08);
  border-radius: 14px 0 0 0;
  overflow-y: auto; z-index: 9998;

}
.cfm-drawer-title {

}

.cfm-drawer-toggle.disabled { opacity: 0.45; cursor: default; }
.cfm-drawer-empty {
  padding: 1rem;
  color: #8a9bb0;
  font-size: 0.82rem;
  line-height: 1.55;
}
.cfm-track-item {
  display: grid; grid-template-columns: 22px minmax(0, 1fr) auto auto; align-items: center; gap: 0.65rem;
  padding: 0.65rem 1rem; cursor: pointer;

.cfm-track-item.skipped .cfm-track-name { text-decoration: line-through; }
.cfm-track-marker {

.cfm-track-dot {

.cfm-track-item.playing .cfm-track-dot { display: block; }
.cfm-track-item.playing .cfm-track-num { display: none; }
.cfm-track-info { flex: 1; min-width: 0; }
.cfm-track-name {

.cfm-track-genre { font-size: 0.67rem; color: #445; margin-top: 0.1rem; }
.cfm-track-fav {

.cfm-track-fav.active { color: #ef4444; }
.cfm-track-skip {

      <div class="mc-intro-tag">Topic 40 — Oversight & Specialty</div>
      <h2>Executing Manual Contracts in a Deployed Environment</h2>
      <p>No contract writing system. No fancy tools. Just a blank SF 1449, a pen (or a PDF editor), and the knowledge to fill it correctly.</p>
    </div>

    

    <div class="mc-tabs">
      <button class="mc-tab active" onclick="showMcTab('learn', this)">📖 Learn</button>
      <button class="mc-tab" onclick="showMcTab('walkthrough', this)">📝 1449 Walkthrough</button>
      <button class="mc-tab" onclick="showMcTab('tools', this)">🔧 Builder Tools</button>
      <button class="mc-tab" onclick="showMcTab('lookup', this)">🔍 Look It Up</button>
    </div>

    <!-- ══════════════════════════════════════════════ LEARN ══ -->
    <div id="mc-learn" class="mc-panel active">

      <!-- 1 -->
      <div class="learn-section">
        <h3><span class="section-num">1</span> When You Write Manual Contracts</h3>
        <div class="learn-body">
          <p>In a deployed or contingency environment, you may not have access to a contract writing system. No ConWrite, no SPS, no PD2. You have a blank SF 1449 in PDF form (or printed copies), and you are the system. The contract is still a contract. It still needs to be legally sufficient. The same FAR, DFARS, and supplemental requirements still apply. The only thing that changes is the tool you are using to produce the document.</p>

          <p>The SF 1449, "Solicitation/Contract/Order for Commercial Products and Services," is the standard form for commercial acquisitions under FAR Part 12. It covers the first two pages of your contract and award document. Everything after those two pages is the substance of your contract: your statement of work, your clauses, your delivery terms, and your attachments.</p>

          <div class="highlight-box">
            <strong>Know your forms.</strong> The SF 1449 is for commercial products and services. The SF 1442 is for construction. The SF 1155 (Order for Supplies or Services) can be simpler for some manual actions. Which form you use depends on the nature of the requirement. For modifications, you use the SF 30 regardless of which award form you started with.
          </div>

          <div class="highlight-box tip">
            <strong>DLA has a solid walkthrough</strong> of the first two pages of the SF 1449, block by block. Before going further, review their training on how to read a solicitation/contract/order for commercial products and services. <a href="https://www.dla.mil/Small-Business/Resource-Center/Training-Resources/Details/Article/4181220/how-to-read-a-solicitationcontractorder-for-commercial-products-and-services-sf/" target="_blank" rel="noopener" style="color:var(--accent);">DLA SF 1449 Training</a>
          </div>
        </div>
      </div>

      <hr class="learn-divider">

      <!-- 2 -->
      <div class="learn-section">
        <h3><span class="section-num">2</span> After the First Two Pages: The UCF as Your Guide</h3>
        <div class="learn-body">
          <p>The first two pages of the SF 1449 are the form itself. Everything after that is the body of your contract. In a normal contract writing system, the software structures this for you. When writing manually, you need a structure yourself. The best one to follow is the Uniform Contract Format (UCF) from FAR 15.204-1.</p>

          <p>Even though FAR Part 15 negotiated procedures may not apply to your contingency buy, the UCF is a clean, logical way to organize contract content. Here is the full section breakdown, and which ones you actually need for a typical manual contract:</p>

          <table class="ucf-table">
            <thead>
              <tr>
                <th>Section</th>
                <th>Title</th>
                <th>Manual Contract?</th>
                <th>Why / Why Not</th>
              </tr>
            </thead>
            <tbody>
              <tr>
                <td><strong>A</strong></td>
                <td>Solicitation/Contract Form</td>
                <td><span class="ucf-use no">Built In</span></td>
                <td>This is the SF 1449 itself. The form is your Section A.</td>
              </tr>
              <tr>
                <td><strong>B</strong></td>
                <td>Supplies or Services and Prices/Costs</td>
                <td><span class="ucf-use no">Built In</span></td>
                <td>Blocks 19-24 of the 1449 cover this. Fill in the schedule on the form.</td>
              </tr>
              <tr class="used">
                <td><strong>C</strong></td>
                <td>Description / Specifications / SOW</td>
                <td><span class="ucf-use yes">Include</span></td>
                <td>Your PWS, SOW, or specifications. Put the whole thing in. In a deployed environment, key documents get lost. Having the full SOW inside your contract means it travels with the contract.</td>
              </tr>
              <tr>
                <td><strong>D</strong></td>
                <td>Packaging and Marking</td>
                <td><span class="ucf-use no">Skip</span></td>
                <td>Rarely relevant in a contingency environment unless you are buying supplies with specific packaging requirements.</td>
              </tr>
              <tr>
                <td><strong>E</strong></td>
                <td>Inspection and Acceptance</td>
                <td><span class="ucf-use no">Covered</span></td>
                <td>Covered by FAR 52.212-4, which should be in your Section I clauses.</td>
              </tr>
              <tr class="used">
                <td><strong>F</strong></td>
                <td>Deliveries or Performance</td>
                <td><span class="ucf-use yes">Include</span></td>
                <td>Your delivery schedule or period of performance. When does it start, when does it end, where does performance happen.</td>
              </tr>
              <tr>
                <td><strong>G</strong></td>
                <td>Contract Administration Data</td>
                <td><span class="ucf-use no">Skip</span></td>
                <td>Not typically needed for a contingency contract.</td>
              </tr>
              <tr class="used">
                <td><strong>H</strong></td>
                <td>Special Contract Requirements</td>
                <td><span class="ucf-use sometimes">Sometimes</span></td>
                <td>Base access instructions, security requirements, or location-specific operational constraints. If your deployed base has these, put them here.</td>
              </tr>
              <tr class="used">
                <td><strong>I</strong></td>
                <td>Contract Clauses</td>
                <td><span class="ucf-use yes">Include</span></td>
                <td>This is the section most people struggle with. At minimum you need 52.212-4 and a payment instruction clause. Use the KTHQ clause matrix or build your own.</td>
              </tr>
              <tr class="used">
                <td><strong>J</strong></td>
                <td>List of Attachments</td>
                <td><span class="ucf-use yes">Include</span></td>
                <td>Just a list of what is attached. Maps, diagrams, GFP lists, etc.</td>
              </tr>
              <tr>
                <td><strong>K</strong></td>
                <td>Reps, Certs, Other Statements</td>
                <td><span class="ucf-use no">Solicitation</span></td>
                <td>These were in your solicitation. Not needed on the award document.</td>
              </tr>
              <tr>
                <td><strong>L</strong></td>
                <td>Instructions, Conditions, Notices</td>
                <td><span class="ucf-use no">Solicitation</span></td>
                <td>Same as K. Solicitation-only.</td>
              </tr>
              <tr>
                <td><strong>M</strong></td>
                <td>Evaluation Factors</td>
                <td><span class="ucf-use no">Solicitation</span></td>
                <td>Same as K and L. Evaluation criteria are part of the solicitation, not the award.</td>
              </tr>
            </tbody>
          </table>

          <div class="highlight-box tip">
            <strong>So what do you actually need to attach to your 1449?</strong> Sections C, F, I, and J. Add H if your base has access or operational requirements. That is your contract. Everything else is either built into the form, covered by a clause, or was only relevant during the solicitation phase.
          </div>
        </div>
      </div>

      <hr class="learn-divider">

      <!-- 3 -->
      <div class="learn-section">
        <h3><span class="section-num">3</span> Section I: Getting Your Clauses Right</h3>
        <div class="learn-body">
          <p>Section I is where most manual contracts go wrong. Without a contract writing system auto-populating your clauses, you need to know which clauses apply and add them yourself.</p>

          <div class="highlight-box">
            <strong>The non-negotiable minimum for a commercial contract:</strong> FAR 52.212-4 (Contract Terms and Conditions, Commercial Products and Commercial Services). This single clause covers inspection, acceptance, assignment, disputes, payment terms, warranty, limitation of liability, termination, and more. If you put nothing else in your contract, 52.212-4 must be there.
          </div>

          <p>Beyond 52.212-4, you need a payment instruction clause. How is the contractor getting paid? This is the question that determines what else goes in Section I.</p>

          <div class="highlight-box warn">
            <strong>Payment by GPC:</strong> If you are in a situation where you are writing manual contracts, you are probably paying by cash or GPC. DAFI 64-117 authorizes the GPC as a method of payment against contracts. If you are paying by GPC, your clauses should reflect that. This is the simplest path in a deployed environment.
          </div>

          <div class="highlight-box">
            <strong>Payment by electronic funds (WAWF):</strong> You can do manual contracts with electronic payment through WAWF via DFAS. But this means you need your WAWF clause in the contract (DFARS 252.232-7006 or applicable), AND you must upload your contract into EDA via PIEE. If the contract is not in EDA, your contractor will not get paid through WAWF. Period.
          </div>

          <div class="highlight-box tip">
            <strong>Use the clause matrix.</strong> We have a <a href="provisions-clauses-commercial.html" style="color:var(--accent);">clause matrix here at KTHQ</a> built from the FAR 12.205 tables. Under the RFO, the old "master clauses" (52.212-5 and 52.212-3) are gone. The applicable clauses for commercial acquisitions now come directly from the FAR 12.205 tables (Tables 12-2, 12-3, and 12-4). Use the matrix to identify which ones apply to your buy, then list them in Section I. Build your own tailored matrix for your deployed operation so you can reuse it across multiple actions.
          </div>
        </div>
      </div>

      <hr class="learn-divider">

      <!-- 4 -->
      <div class="learn-section">
        <h3><span class="section-num">4</span> You Still Have to Upload to EDA</h3>
        <div class="learn-body">
          <p>This catches people off guard. You wrote the contract by hand (or on a PDF). You signed it. The contractor signed it. It is a binding contract. But if you do not upload it into EDA (Electronic Document Access) through PIEE, the contract does not exist in the official system of record.</p>

          <div class="highlight-box warn">
            <strong>If you are paying via WAWF, this is critical.</strong> DFAS processes payments through WAWF, which validates against EDA. No contract in EDA means no payment processing. Your contractor delivered the dumpsters, did the work, and has a signed contract, but cannot get paid because the contract is not in the system. Upload it.
          </div>

          <div class="highlight-box tip">
            <strong>Even if you are paying by GPC,</strong> upload the contract to EDA. It is the official system of record for contract documents. An executed contract that only exists as a scanned PDF on someone's laptop is a contract that disappears when that laptop gets lost, damaged, or rotated out with the next unit. EDA is permanent. Use it.
          </div>
        </div>
      </div>

      <hr class="learn-divider">

      <!-- 5 -->
      <div class="learn-section">
        <h3><span class="section-num">5</span> Modifications: The Red Text Method</h3>
        <div class="learn-body">
          <p>Manual contracts get modified with manual SF 30s. The same form, done the same way, just without a contract writing system generating it for you. The key challenge with manual modifications is tracking what changed across the life of the contract.</p>

          <p>Here is a method that works well and produces something close to a conformed copy by the time the contract closes out:</p>

          <div class="highlight-box tip">
            <strong>Modification 1:</strong> Start with your base contract content. All new or changed text from Mod 1 goes in <span style="color:#ef4444;">red</span>. Everything else stays black. This makes it immediately obvious what Mod 1 did.
          </div>

          <div class="highlight-box tip">
            <strong>Modification 2:</strong> Take your Mod 1 document. Change the Mod 1 red text to black (it is now part of the baseline). Add Mod 2 changes in <span style="color:#ef4444;">red</span>. Now anyone reading the document can see what is new from Mod 2 and what was already incorporated.
          </div>

          <div class="highlight-box tip">
            <strong>By the last modification,</strong> you have a running document that contains the entire history of the contract. All previous changes are in black (baseline). Only the most recent changes are in red. It reads like a conformed copy of the contract. Not mandatory, but when you close out the file or hand it off to the next rotation, whoever inherits the contract can read one document and know exactly what the contract looks like today.
          </div>

          <div class="highlight-box">
            <strong>What goes in a typical deployed modification?</strong> Option exercises, period of performance extensions, quantity changes, price adjustments, and scope additions are the most common. Each mod should clearly state what it changes, reference the specific blocks or sections affected, and carry forward the full contract content so the document remains self-contained.
          </div>
        </div>
      </div>

      <hr class="learn-divider">

      <!-- 6 -->
      <div class="learn-section">
        <h3><span class="section-num">6</span> Accuracy Matters More When There Is No System Checking Your Work</h3>
        <div class="learn-body">
          <p>A contract writing system catches a lot of errors for you. Wrong CAGE code format, missing required clauses, inconsistent dollar amounts. When you are doing it manually, there is no system-level validation. You are the quality control.</p>

          <div class="highlight-box warn">
            <strong>Things to double-check on every manual contract:</strong>
            <br><br>
            The contract number follows proper formatting. NAICS code and size standard match the requirement. The total award amount in Block 26 matches the line items in Blocks 19-24. The CAGE code and DUNS/UEI are correct for the contractor. The period of performance dates are right. Clause citations are accurate and current. The solicitation number in Block 5 matches what you issued. The payment instructions actually work (GPC charge, or WAWF with the contract in EDA). Your signature and the contractor's signature are both present.
          </div>

          <p>Read through the completed contract as if someone else wrote it and you are reviewing it. If anything does not add up, fix it before execution. There is no "the system will catch that" safety net here.</p>
        </div>
      </div>

    </div>

  <script>
    function showMcTab(id, btn) {
      document.querySelectorAll('.mc-panel').forEach(function(p) { p.classList.remove('active'); });
      document.querySelectorAll('.mc-tab').forEach(function(t) { t.classList.remove('active'); });

    }

    var mcNotes = {
      reqno: {
        title: "Block 1: Requisition Number",
        body: "Your PR number. In a deployed environment, this may come from a manual PR system or your unit's tracking sheet. Whatever numbering system your office uses, put it here. If you do not have a formal PR system, create a log and use sequential numbering so you can track requirements back to their source."
      },
      contractno: {
        title: "Block 2: Contract Number",
        body: "Your contract number. In a contract writing system, this is auto-generated. When writing manually, you need to follow your organization's contract numbering convention.<br><br><strong>Standard DoD format:</strong> The contract number follows PII (Procurement Instrument Identification) rules per DFARS 204.16. It includes your DODAAC, fiscal year, instrument type (P for purchase order, C for contract, etc.), and a sequential number.<br><br><strong>Avoid number collisions.</strong> If a contract writing system is eventually introduced to your AOR, it will automatically start issuing numbers at 0001, 0002, 0003. If you already used those, you have a conflict. To prevent this, add a distinguishing character to your manual sequence. For example: FA460024P<strong>Z</strong>001, FA460024P<strong>M</strong>001, or even use your initials like FA460024P<strong>NH</strong>01. Pick a convention and stick with it. That way, your manual numbers will never overlap with system-generated ones.<br><br>If you are not sure what your DODAAC is or what numbering sequence your office is using, check with your flight chief or the previous rotation's contracting team. Using someone else's sequence or making up a format will cause problems downstream when the contract goes into EDA."
      },
      awarddate: {
        title: "Block 3: Award/Effective Date",
        body: "The date the contract becomes effective. In most cases this is the date both parties sign. Do not backdate contracts. If you need services to start on a specific date, make that the start date in your period of performance (Section F), not the award date."
      },
      solno: {
        title: "Block 5: Solicitation Number",
        body: "Your solicitation number. This should match whatever you issued as the solicitation document. Even in a contingency environment, you issued something (an RFP, RFQ, or request for offers) and it had a number. That number goes here. The contract number and solicitation number will usually share the same base, with different instrument type codes."
      },
      offerdue: {
        title: "Block 8: Offer Due Date/Local Time",
        body: "When offers were due. This is a solicitation block, so on the award document it reflects when the deadline was. In a deployed environment, be specific about the time zone. \"1600L\" means 1600 local time at the place of performance. If you are coordinating across time zones, spell it out."
      },
      issuedby: {
        title: "Block 9: Issued By",
        body: "Your contracting office. Include the unit, office symbol, and mailing address. In a deployed environment, this is usually your APO/FPO address. Make sure this matches your DODAAC registration. If your unit just stood up a new contracting office and the DODAAC has not been registered yet, get that sorted before you start issuing contracts."
      },
      acquisition: {
        title: "Block 10: This Acquisition Is",
        body: "Check the appropriate box. The Rule of Two still applies in a deployed environment. If two or more small businesses can meet the requirement at competitive prices, quality, and delivery, you must set aside per FAR 19.104-1.<br><br>Include your NAICS code and size standard. If you are buying waste removal services, that is NAICS 562111 (Solid Waste Collection). Get the right code. A wrong NAICS does not become right just because you are deployed."
      },
      method: {
        title: "Block 14: Method of Solicitation",
        body: "RFQ for simplified acquisitions. RFP if you are evaluating offers under competitive procedures. IFB for sealed bidding (rare in contingency). Check the one that matches how you actually solicited. If you posted a request and evaluated responses, that is an RFP."
      },
      deliverto: {
        title: "Block 15: Deliver To",
        body: "Where the supplies are delivered or where services are performed. In a deployed environment, this is your base or operating location. Include the COR's name and contact info so the contractor knows who to coordinate with on the ground."
      },
      contractor: {
        title: "Block 17a: Contractor/Offeror",
        body: "The contractor's name, address, and contact information. Verify the contractor's legal name. In many deployed environments, local contractors may not have a CAGE code or UEI. If they are a foreign vendor operating outside the U.S., document what you can and follow your theater's guidance on contractor registration.<br><br>The CAGE code in Block 17a (Code field) is important for EDA and payment processing. If the contractor does not have one, your office may need to help them get registered, or your theater may have a process for this."
      },
      payment: {
        title: "Block 18a: Payment Will Be Made By",
        body: "How the contractor gets paid. This is critical.<br><br><strong>GPC:</strong> If paying by Government Purchase Card, state it here. DAFI 64-117 authorizes GPC as a method of payment against contracts. This is the simplest option in a deployed environment.<br><br><strong>WAWF/DFAS:</strong> If paying electronically through WAWF, list the DFAS payment office and cage code. But remember: the contract must be uploaded to EDA via PIEE or DFAS cannot process the payment. No EDA entry means no payment, regardless of what this block says.<br><br>Whatever you put here needs to be consistent with your payment clause in Section I."
      },
      schedule: {
        title: "Blocks 19-24: Schedule of Supplies/Services",
        body: "Your line items. Each CLIN gets a row. Include the item number, description, quantity, unit of issue, unit price, and extended amount.<br><br><strong>For services:</strong> Reference your PWS/SOW in the description (e.g., \"Per PWS, Section C\"). Include the period of performance for each CLIN. If you have a base period and options, make them separate CLINs so you can exercise options individually via modification.<br><br><strong>Math check:</strong> Quantity times unit price must equal amount. Total of all amounts must equal Block 26. No contract writing system is checking this for you. Get it right."
      },
      total: {
        title: "Block 26: Total Award Amount",
        body: "The total obligated amount at time of award. For a contract with options, this should reflect only the base period amount that is being funded and obligated at award, not the total potential value including all options.<br><br>In this example, only the base period (CLIN 0001, $25,200) is obligated. Option Period 1 will be obligated later via modification if the option is exercised. The total in Block 26 is $25,200, not $51,300."
      },
      award: {
        title: "Block 29: Award of Contract",
        body: "Check this block and reference \"SEE SCHEDULE\" for the items accepted. This block indicates that the Government is accepting the contractor's offer. When both Block 29 is checked and both parties have signed (Blocks 30 and 31), you have a binding contract."
      },
      cosig: {
        title: "Block 31: Contracting Officer Signature",
        body: "Your signature, printed name, title, and date. This is the block that makes it a contract. Only a warranted contracting officer can sign here.<br><br>In a deployed environment, you may be signing a physical copy with a pen, or using a digital signature on a PDF. Either is acceptable. What matters is that a warranted CO signed it. If you are a contract specialist without a warrant, you cannot sign Block 31. Period.<br><br>Make sure the date here matches or follows the contractor's signature date in Block 30c. You cannot accept an offer before it was made."
      }
    };

    function showMcNote(key) {
      document.querySelectorAll('.mock-click').forEach(function(c) { c.classList.remove('active'); });
      document.querySelectorAll('.mock-click[data-note="' + key + '"]').forEach(function(c) { c.classList.add('active'); });
      document.getElementById('mcNoteTitle').textContent = mcNotes[key].title;
      document.getElementById('mcNoteBody').innerHTML = mcNotes[key].body;
      document.getElementById('mcOverlay').classList.add('visible');
    }
    function hideMcNote() {
      document.getElementById('mcOverlay').classList.remove('visible');
      document.querySelectorAll('.mock-click').forEach(function(c) { c.classList.remove('active'); });
    }
