    function addClin() {
      var id = 'clin-' + clinCount++;
      var row = document.createElement('div');
      row.className = 'clin-row';
      row.id = id;
      row.innerHTML = '<input type="text" placeholder="0002" /><input type="text" class="clin-desc" placeholder="Description" /><input type="number" placeholder="Qty" min="0" step="1" /><input type="text" placeholder="EA" /><input type="text" placeholder="$0.00" /><button class="clause-remove" onclick="removeClin(\'' + id + '\')">×</button>';
      document.getElementById('clin-list').appendChild(row);
    }
    function removeClin(id) {
      var el = document.getElementById(id);
      if (el) el.remove();
    }

    function addClause() {
      var id = 'clause-' + clauseCount++;
      var row = document.createElement('div');
      row.className = 'clause-row';
      row.id = id;
      row.innerHTML = '<input type="text" placeholder="Clause #" /><input type="text" placeholder="Clause Title" /><button class="clause-remove" onclick="removeClause(\'' + id + '\')">×</button>';
      document.getElementById('clause-list').appendChild(row);
    }
    function removeClause(id) {
      var el = document.getElementById(id);
      if (el) el.remove();
    }
    function addAttach() {
      attachCount++;
      var id = 'attach-' + attachCount;
      var row = document.createElement('div');
      row.className = 'attach-row';
      row.id = id;
      row.innerHTML = '<input type="text" value="J-' + attachCount + '" placeholder="#" style="text-align:center;" /><input type="text" placeholder="Attachment description" /><button class="clause-remove" onclick="removeAttach(\'' + id + '\')">×</button>';
      document.getElementById('attach-list').appendChild(row);
    }
    function removeAttach(id) {
      var el = document.getElementById(id);
      if (el) el.remove();
    }

    function escHtml(s) {
      var d = document.createElement('div');
      d.textContent = s;
      return d.innerHTML;
    }

    function fmtDate(d) {
      if (!d) return '(TBD)';
      var parts = d.split('-');
      var months = ['Jan','Feb','Mar','Apr','May','Jun','Jul','Aug','Sep','Oct','Nov','Dec'];
      return parseInt(parts[2]) + ' ' + months[parseInt(parts[1])-1] + ' ' + parts[0];
    }

    function parseDollar(s) {
      if (!s) return 0;
      return parseFloat(s.replace(/[^0-9.\-]/g, '')) || 0;
    }

    function fmtDollar(n) {
      return '$' + n.toFixed(2).replace(/\B(?=(\d{3})+(?!\d))/g, ',');
    }

    function collectFormData() {
      var data = {
        contractNo: document.getElementById('bld-contractno').value || '(Contract Number)',
        contractor: document.getElementById('bld-contractor').value || '(Contractor Name)',
        clins: [],
        cTitle: document.getElementById('bld-c-title').value,
        cBody: document.getElementById('bld-c-body').value,
        fType: document.getElementById('bld-f-type').value,
        fStart: document.getElementById('bld-f-start').value,
        fEnd: document.getElementById('bld-f-end').value,
        fDelivery: document.getElementById('bld-f-delivery').value,
        fPlace: document.getElementById('bld-f-place').value,
        fBody: document.getElementById('bld-f-body').value,
        hBody: document.getElementById('bld-h-body').value,
        clauses: [],
        attachments: []
      };
      document.querySelectorAll('#clin-list .clin-row').forEach(function(row) {
        var inputs = row.querySelectorAll('input');
        var clin = inputs[0].value.trim();
        var desc = inputs[1].value.trim();
        var qty = parseFloat(inputs[2].value) || 0;
        var unit = inputs[3].value.trim();
        var unitPrice = parseDollar(inputs[4].value);
        if (clin || desc) data.clins.push({ clin: clin, desc: desc, qty: qty, unit: unit, unitPrice: unitPrice });
      });
      document.querySelectorAll('#clause-list .clause-row').forEach(function(row) {
        var inputs = row.querySelectorAll('input');
        var num = inputs[0].value.trim();
        var title = inputs[1].value.trim();
        if (num || title) data.clauses.push({ num: num, title: title });
      });
      document.querySelectorAll('#attach-list .attach-row').forEach(function(row) {
        var inputs = row.querySelectorAll('input');
        var num = inputs[0].value.trim();
        var desc = inputs[1].value.trim();
        if (num || desc) data.attachments.push({ num: num, desc: desc });
      });
      return data;
    }

    function buildSectionHTML(d) {
      var html = '';
      html += '<div style="font-family: Arial, Helvetica, sans-serif; font-size: 11px; color: #000; line-height: 1.6; max-width: 700px; margin: 0 auto; padding: 20px;">';

      html += '<div style="text-align:center; border-bottom:2px solid #000; padding-bottom:8px; margin-bottom:20px;">';
      html += '<div style="font-size:13px; font-weight:bold;">CONTINUATION OF SF 1449</div>';
      html += '<div style="font-size:11px; margin-top:3px;">Contract No. ' + escHtml(d.contractNo) + '</div>';
      html += '<div style="font-size:10px; color:#555;">Contractor: ' + escHtml(d.contractor) + '</div>';
      html += '</div>';

      // Schedule / CLINs
      if (d.clins.length > 0) {
        html += '<div style="margin-bottom:24px;">';
        html += '<div style="font-size:13px; font-weight:bold; border-bottom:1px solid #999; padding-bottom:4px; margin-bottom:8px;">SCHEDULE — CONTRACT LINE ITEMS</div>';
        html += '<table style="border-collapse:collapse; width:100%; font-size:10.5px;">';
        html += '<tr style="border-bottom:1px solid #999;"><th style="text-align:left; padding:4px 6px; font-weight:bold;">CLIN</th><th style="text-align:left; padding:4px 6px; font-weight:bold;">Description</th><th style="text-align:right; padding:4px 6px; font-weight:bold;">Qty</th><th style="text-align:left; padding:4px 6px; font-weight:bold;">Unit</th><th style="text-align:right; padding:4px 6px; font-weight:bold;">Unit Price</th><th style="text-align:right; padding:4px 6px; font-weight:bold;">Extended</th></tr>';
        var grandTotal = 0;
        d.clins.forEach(function(c) {
          var ext = c.qty * c.unitPrice;
          grandTotal += ext;
          html += '<tr style="border-bottom:1px solid #e0e0e0;">';
          html += '<td style="padding:4px 6px;">' + escHtml(c.clin) + '</td>';
          html += '<td style="padding:4px 6px;">' + escHtml(c.desc) + '</td>';
          html += '<td style="padding:4px 6px; text-align:right;">' + (c.qty || '') + '</td>';
          html += '<td style="padding:4px 6px;">' + escHtml(c.unit) + '</td>';
          html += '<td style="padding:4px 6px; text-align:right;">' + (c.unitPrice ? fmtDollar(c.unitPrice) : '') + '</td>';
          html += '<td style="padding:4px 6px; text-align:right;">' + (ext ? fmtDollar(ext) : '') + '</td>';
          html += '</tr>';
        });
        html += '<tr style="border-top:2px solid #000;"><td colspan="5" style="padding:4px 6px; font-weight:bold; text-align:right;">Total:</td><td style="padding:4px 6px; font-weight:bold; text-align:right;">' + fmtDollar(grandTotal) + '</td></tr>';
        html += '</table>';
        html += '</div>';
      }

      html += '<div style="margin-bottom:24px;">';
      html += '<div style="font-size:13px; font-weight:bold; border-bottom:1px solid #999; padding-bottom:4px; margin-bottom:8px;">SECTION C — DESCRIPTION / SPECIFICATIONS / STATEMENT OF WORK</div>';
      if (d.cTitle) html += '<div style="font-weight:bold; margin-bottom:6px;">' + escHtml(d.cTitle) + '</div>';
      if (d.cBody) {
        d.cBody.split('\n').forEach(function(p) {
          if (p.trim()) html += '<p style="margin:0 0 8px;">' + escHtml(p) + '</p>';
        });
      } else {
        html += '<p style="color:#999;">(No content provided)</p>';
      }
      html += '</div>';

      html += '<div style="margin-bottom:24px;">';
      html += '<div style="font-size:13px; font-weight:bold; border-bottom:1px solid #999; padding-bottom:4px; margin-bottom:8px;">SECTION F — DELIVERIES OR PERFORMANCE</div>';
      if (d.fType === 'pop') {
        html += '<table style="border-collapse:collapse; font-size:11px; margin-bottom:8px;">';
        html += '<tr><td style="padding:3px 12px 3px 0; font-weight:bold;">Period of Performance:</td><td>' + fmtDate(d.fStart) + ' through ' + fmtDate(d.fEnd) + '</td></tr>';
        if (d.fPlace) html += '<tr><td style="padding:3px 12px 3px 0; font-weight:bold;">Place of Performance:</td><td>' + escHtml(d.fPlace) + '</td></tr>';
        html += '</table>';
      } else {
        if (d.fDelivery) {
          d.fDelivery.split('\n').forEach(function(p) {
            if (p.trim()) html += '<p style="margin:0 0 8px;">' + escHtml(p) + '</p>';
          });
        }
        if (d.fPlace) {
          html += '<table style="border-collapse:collapse; font-size:11px; margin-bottom:8px;">';
          html += '<tr><td style="padding:3px 12px 3px 0; font-weight:bold;">Place of Delivery:</td><td>' + escHtml(d.fPlace) + '</td></tr>';
          html += '</table>';
        }
      }
      if (d.fBody) {
        d.fBody.split('\n').forEach(function(p) {
          if (p.trim()) html += '<p style="margin:0 0 8px;">' + escHtml(p) + '</p>';
        });
      }
      html += '</div>';

      if (d.hBody && d.hBody.trim()) {
        html += '<div style="margin-bottom:24px;">';
        html += '<div style="font-size:13px; font-weight:bold; border-bottom:1px solid #999; padding-bottom:4px; margin-bottom:8px;">SECTION H — SPECIAL CONTRACT REQUIREMENTS</div>';
        d.hBody.split('\n').forEach(function(p) {
          if (p.trim()) html += '<p style="margin:0 0 8px;">' + escHtml(p) + '</p>';
        });
        html += '</div>';
      }

      html += '<div style="margin-bottom:24px;">';
      html += '<div style="font-size:13px; font-weight:bold; border-bottom:1px solid #999; padding-bottom:4px; margin-bottom:8px;">SECTION I — CONTRACT CLAUSES</div>';
      html += '<p style="margin:0 0 10px;">The following clauses apply per FAR 12.205 and are incorporated by reference:</p>';
      if (d.clauses.length > 0) {
        html += '<table style="border-collapse:collapse; width:100%; font-size:10.5px;">';
        html += '<tr style="border-bottom:1px solid #999;"><th style="text-align:left; padding:4px 8px; font-weight:bold;">Clause</th><th style="text-align:left; padding:4px 8px; font-weight:bold;">Title</th></tr>';
        d.clauses.forEach(function(c) {
          html += '<tr style="border-bottom:1px solid #e0e0e0;"><td style="padding:4px 8px; white-space:nowrap;">' + escHtml(c.num) + '</td><td style="padding:4px 8px;">' + escHtml(c.title) + '</td></tr>';
        });
        html += '</table>';
      } else {
        html += '<p style="color:#999;">(No clauses added)</p>';
      }
      html += '</div>';

      if (d.attachments.length > 0) {
        html += '<div style="margin-bottom:24px;">';
        html += '<div style="font-size:13px; font-weight:bold; border-bottom:1px solid #999; padding-bottom:4px; margin-bottom:8px;">SECTION J — LIST OF ATTACHMENTS</div>';
        html += '<table style="border-collapse:collapse; width:100%; font-size:10.5px;">';
        html += '<tr style="border-bottom:1px solid #999;"><th style="text-align:left; padding:4px 8px; font-weight:bold;">No.</th><th style="text-align:left; padding:4px 8px; font-weight:bold;">Description</th></tr>';
        d.attachments.forEach(function(a) {
          html += '<tr style="border-bottom:1px solid #e0e0e0;"><td style="padding:4px 8px; white-space:nowrap;">' + escHtml(a.num) + '</td><td style="padding:4px 8px;">' + escHtml(a.desc) + '</td></tr>';
        });
        html += '</table>';
        html += '</div>';
      }

      html += '<div style="border-top:1px solid #999; padding-top:6px; margin-top:24px; font-size:9px; color:#777; text-align:center;">End of Continuation — ' + escHtml(d.contractNo) + '</div>';
      html += '</div>';
      return html;
    }

    function showPreview() {
      var d = collectFormData();
      var container = document.getElementById('preview-container');
      document.getElementById('section-preview').innerHTML = buildSectionHTML(d);
      container.style.display = 'block';
      container.scrollIntoView({ behavior: 'smooth' });
    }

    function generatePDF() {
      var d = collectFormData();
      var target = document.getElementById('pdf-content');
      target.innerHTML = buildSectionHTML(d);
      target.className = 'rendering';

      var filename = d.contractNo.replace(/[^a-zA-Z0-9\-]/g, '_') + '_Sections.pdf';

      html2pdf().set({
        margin: [0.5, 0.6, 0.5, 0.6],
        filename: filename,
        html2canvas: { scale: 2, useCORS: true },
        jsPDF: { unit: 'in', format: 'letter', orientation: 'portrait' },
        pagebreak: { mode: ['avoid-all', 'css', 'legacy'] }
      }).from(target).save().then(function() {
        target.className = '';
        target.innerHTML = '';
      });
    }
  </script>

.cfm-brand {
  display: flex; align-items: center; gap: 0.5rem;
  padding: 0 1.1rem; border-right: 1px solid rgba(255,255,255,0.06);
  min-width: 130px; flex-shrink: 0;
}
.cfm-brand-logo {
  font-family: 'Rajdhani', sans-serif; font-size: 0.95rem; font-weight: 700;
  color: #fff; letter-spacing: 0.5px; white-space: nowrap;
}
.cfm-brand-logo span { color: var(--cfm-accent, #4a9eff); }
.cfm-on-air {
  font-size: 0.55rem; font-weight: 700; letter-spacing: 1.5px;
  text-transform: uppercase; color: #ef4444;
  background: rgba(239,68,68,0.12); border: 1px solid rgba(239,68,68,0.3);
  border-radius: 3px; padding: 0.1rem 0.35rem;
  animation: cfm-pulse 2s ease-in-out infinite;
  transition: color 0.3s, background 0.3s, border-color 0.3s;
}
.cfm-on-air.off-air {
  color: #445; background: rgba(255,255,255,0.04); border-color: rgba(255,255,255,0.1);
  animation: none;
}
@keyframes cfm-pulse { 0%,100% { opacity:1; } 50% { opacity:0.5; } }

.cfm-song-info {
  display: flex; align-items: center; gap: 0.75rem;
  padding: 0 1.1rem; border-right: 1px solid rgba(255,255,255,0.06);
  min-width: 210px; max-width: 260px; flex-shrink: 0;
}
.cfm-art {
  width: 40px; height: 40px; border-radius: 6px; flex-shrink: 0;
  display: flex; align-items: center; justify-content: center;
  font-size: 1.2rem;
  background: rgba(255,255,255,0.06);
  border: 1px solid rgba(255,255,255,0.08);
  transition: background 0.3s;
}
.cfm-meta { flex: 1; min-width: 0; }
.cfm-meta-title {
  font-size: 0.8rem; font-weight: 600; color: #e2e8f0;
  white-space: nowrap; overflow: hidden; text-overflow: ellipsis;
}
.cfm-meta-sub {
  font-size: 0.68rem; color: #556; margin-top: 0.1rem;
  white-space: nowrap; overflow: hidden; text-overflow: ellipsis;
}
.cfm-meta-genre {
  display: inline-block; font-size: 0.6rem; font-weight: 700;
  color: var(--cfm-accent, #4a9eff);
  background: rgba(74,158,255,0.1); border-radius: 3px;
  padding: 0.1rem 0.35rem; margin-top: 0.15rem; letter-spacing: 0.5px;
}
.cfm-heart {
  background: none; border: none; cursor: pointer; font-size: 1rem;
  color: #445; transition: color 0.2s, transform 0.15s; flex-shrink: 0; padding: 0.2rem;
}
.cfm-heart.active { color: #ef4444; }
.cfm-heart:hover { transform: scale(1.2); }

.cfm-controls {
  display: flex; align-items: center; gap: 0.5rem;
  padding: 0 1.25rem; border-right: 1px solid rgba(255,255,255,0.06); flex-shrink: 0;
}
.cfm-btn {
  background: none; border: none; cursor: pointer;
  color: #8a9bb0; font-size: 0.85rem; padding: 0.4rem;
  border-radius: 50%; transition: color 0.18s, background 0.18s, transform 0.15s;
  display: flex; align-items: center; justify-content: center;
  width: 30px; height: 30px;
}
.cfm-btn:hover { color: #fff; background: rgba(255,255,255,0.08); }
.cfm-btn.cfm-play-btn {
  width: 38px; height: 38px; font-size: 1rem;
  background: var(--cfm-accent, #4a9eff); color: #040d1f;
  border-radius: 50%; transition: all 0.18s;
}
.cfm-btn.cfm-play-btn:hover { transform: scale(1.08); filter: brightness(1.15); }
.cfm-btn.cfm-active { color: var(--cfm-accent, #4a9eff); }

.cfm-progress-zone {
  flex: 1; display: flex; align-items: center; gap: 0.6rem;
  padding: 0 1.1rem; min-width: 0;
}
.cfm-time { font-size: 0.68rem; color: #445; flex-shrink: 0; min-width: 32px; }
.cfm-time.right { text-align: right; }
.cfm-bar-wrap { flex: 1; position: relative; height: 4px; cursor: pointer; }
.cfm-bar-bg {
  position: absolute; inset: 0; border-radius: 4px;
  background: rgba(255,255,255,0.08);
}
.cfm-bar-fill {
  position: absolute; left: 0; top: 0; bottom: 0; border-radius: 4px;
  background: var(--cfm-accent, #4a9eff); width: 0%; transition: width 0.1s linear;
}
.cfm-bar-thumb {
  position: absolute; top: 50%; width: 12px; height: 12px;
  border-radius: 50%; background: #fff; transform: translate(-50%, -50%);
  opacity: 0; transition: opacity 0.18s; box-shadow: 0 1px 4px rgba(0,0,0,0.4);
  left: 0%;
}
.cfm-bar-wrap:hover .cfm-bar-thumb { opacity: 1; }

.cfm-volume-zone {
  display: flex; align-items: center; gap: 0.5rem;
  padding: 0 1rem; border-left: 1px solid rgba(255,255,255,0.06); flex-shrink: 0;
}
.cfm-vol-icon { font-size: 0.75rem; color: #445; cursor: pointer; }
input[type=range].cfm-vol-slider {
  -webkit-appearance: none; appearance: none;
  width: 70px; height: 3px; border-radius: 3px;
  background: rgba(255,255,255,0.12); outline: none; cursor: pointer;
}
input[type=range].cfm-vol-slider::-webkit-slider-thumb {
  -webkit-appearance: none; width: 16px; height: 16px; border-radius: 50%;
  background: #fff; cursor: pointer;
}
input[type=range].cfm-vol-slider::-moz-range-thumb {
  width: 12px; height: 12px; border-radius: 50%; background: #fff; cursor: pointer; border: none;
}

.cfm-playlist-btn {
  background: none; border: none; cursor: pointer;
  color: #8a9bb0; font-size: 0.85rem; padding: 0 1rem;
  transition: color 0.18s; flex-shrink: 0; height: 100%;
  display: flex; align-items: center; gap: 0.35rem; font-family: 'Inter', sans-serif;
  border-left: 1px solid rgba(255,255,255,0.06);
}
.cfm-playlist-btn:hover { color: #fff; }
.cfm-playlist-btn.open { color: var(--cfm-accent, #4a9eff); }
.cfm-playlist-text { font-size: 0.72rem; font-weight: 700; }
.cfm-playlist-count {
  display: inline-grid; place-items: center;
  min-width: 1.35rem; height: 1.35rem; padding: 0 0.28rem;
  border-radius: 999px;
  background: rgba(255,255,255,0.08);
  color: #dbe8f7;
  font-size: 0.68rem; font-weight: 800;
}
.cfm-cco-toggle {
  position: relative;
  height: 100%;
  display: inline-flex;
  align-items: center;
  justify-content: center;
  padding: 0 0.85rem;
  border: none;
  border-left: 1px solid rgba(255,255,255,0.06);
  background: rgba(217,154,49,0.04);
  color: #8a9bb0;
  cursor: pointer;
  flex-shrink: 0;
  font-family: 'Inter', sans-serif;
}
.cfm-cco-toggle span {
  border: 1px solid rgba(217,154,49,0.28);
  border-radius: 999px;
  padding: 0.22rem 0.52rem;
  color: #d99a31;
  font-size: 0.68rem;
  font-weight: 900;
  letter-spacing: 0.08em;
}
.cfm-cco-toggle:hover span,
.cfm-cco-toggle:focus-visible span,
.cfm-cco-toggle.active span {
  color: #080905;
  background: #d99a31;
  border-color: #d99a31;
}
.cfm-cco-toggle::after {
  content: attr(data-tip);
  position: absolute;
  right: 0.5rem;
  bottom: calc(100% + 10px);
  width: min(300px, calc(100vw - 24px));
  padding: 0.65rem 0.75rem;
  border: 1px solid rgba(217,154,49,0.34);
  border-radius: 8px;
  background: rgba(6,3,16,0.96);
  color: #dbe8f7;
  box-shadow: 0 14px 34px rgba(0,0,0,0.42);
  font-size: 0.72rem;
  font-weight: 650;
  line-height: 1.45;
  opacity: 0;
  pointer-events: none;
  transform: translateY(4px);
  transition: opacity 0.16s ease, transform 0.16s ease;
}
.cfm-cco-toggle:hover::after,
.cfm-cco-toggle:focus-visible::after {
  opacity: 1;
  transform: translateY(0);
}
.cfm-cco-toggle::after,
.cfm-sb-cco-toggle::after {
  content: none !important;
  display: none !important;
}

/* Playlist drawer */
#cfm-drawer {
  position: fixed; bottom: 68px; right: 0;
  width: 380px; max-height: min(560px, calc(100vh - 92px));
  background: #080414;
  border: 1px solid rgba(255,255,255,0.08);
  border-radius: 14px 0 0 0;
  overflow-y: auto; z-index: 9998;
  display: none;
  box-shadow: -4px -4px 30px rgba(0,0,0,0.5);
}
#cfm-drawer.open { display: block; }
.cfm-drawer-hdr {
  position: sticky; top: 0; z-index: 1;
  padding: 0.85rem 1rem 0.75rem;
  background: #080414;
  border-bottom: 1px solid rgba(255,255,255,0.06);
}
.cfm-drawer-title-row {
  display: flex; align-items: center; justify-content: space-between; gap: 0.75rem;
}
.cfm-drawer-title {
  font-family: 'Rajdhani', sans-serif; font-size: 1rem; font-weight: 700;
  color: #fff; text-transform: uppercase; letter-spacing: 1.2px;
}
.cfm-drawer-count { color: #556; font-size: 0.72rem; font-weight: 700; white-space: nowrap; }
.cfm-drawer-actions {
  display: flex; align-items: center; gap: 0.45rem; margin-top: 0.65rem;
}
.cfm-drawer-toggle {
  border: 1px solid rgba(255,255,255,0.1);
  border-radius: 999px;
  background: rgba(255,255,255,0.035);
  color: #8a9bb0;
  cursor: pointer;
  font: inherit;
  font-size: 0.72rem;
  font-weight: 800;
  padding: 0.35rem 0.65rem;
}
.cfm-drawer-toggle:hover { color: #fff; background: rgba(255,255,255,0.06); }
.cfm-drawer-toggle.active { color: #ef4444; border-color: rgba(239,68,68,0.34); background: rgba(239,68,68,0.08); }
.cfm-drawer-toggle.disabled { opacity: 0.45; cursor: default; }
.cfm-drawer-empty {
  padding: 1rem;
  color: #8a9bb0;
  font-size: 0.82rem;
  line-height: 1.55;
}
.cfm-track-item {
  display: grid; grid-template-columns: 22px minmax(0, 1fr) auto auto; align-items: center; gap: 0.65rem;
  padding: 0.65rem 1rem; cursor: pointer;
  background: #080414;
  transition: background 0.15s; border-bottom: 1px solid rgba(255,255,255,0.04);
}
.cfm-track-item:hover { background: rgba(255,255,255,0.04); }
.cfm-track-item.active { background: #11172d; }
.cfm-track-item.skipped { opacity: 0.58; }
.cfm-track-item.skipped .cfm-track-name { text-decoration: line-through; }
.cfm-track-marker {
  display: grid; place-items: center;
  width: 22px; min-width: 22px;
}
.cfm-track-num {
  font-family: 'Rajdhani', sans-serif; font-size: 0.8rem; color: #334;
  min-width: 18px; text-align: center;
}
.cfm-track-item.active .cfm-track-num { color: var(--cfm-accent, #4a9eff); }
.cfm-track-dot {
  width: 8px; height: 8px; border-radius: 50%;
  animation: cfm-pulse 1s ease-in-out infinite; flex-shrink: 0;
  display: none;
}
.cfm-track-item.playing .cfm-track-dot { display: block; }
.cfm-track-item.playing .cfm-track-num { display: none; }
.cfm-track-info { flex: 1; min-width: 0; }
.cfm-track-name {
  font-size: 0.82rem; font-weight: 600; color: #c0cdd8;
  white-space: nowrap; overflow: hidden; text-overflow: ellipsis;
}
.cfm-track-item.active .cfm-track-name { color: #fff; }
.cfm-track-genre { font-size: 0.67rem; color: #445; margin-top: 0.1rem; }
.cfm-track-fav {
  background: none; border: none; cursor: pointer; font-size: 0.85rem;
  color: #334; transition: color 0.18s; padding: 0.2rem;
}
.cfm-track-fav.active { color: #ef4444; }
.cfm-track-skip {
  border: 1px solid rgba(255,255,255,0.1);
  border-radius: 999px;
  background: rgba(255,255,255,0.035);
  color: #66758a;
  cursor: pointer;
  font: inherit;
  font-size: 0.64rem;
  font-weight: 800;
  line-height: 1;
  padding: 0.32rem 0.48rem;
  text-transform: uppercase;
}
.cfm-track-skip:hover { color: #fff; background: rgba(255,255,255,0.07); }
.cfm-track-skip.active { color: #f59e0b; border-color: rgba(245,158,11,0.34); background: rgba(245,158,11,0.08); }

/* Scrollbar styling for drawer */
#cfm-drawer::-webkit-scrollbar { width: 4px; }
#cfm-drawer::-webkit-scrollbar-track { background: transparent; }
#cfm-drawer::-webkit-scrollbar-thumb { background: rgba(255,255,255,0.1); border-radius: 2px; }

/* Body padding to account for player */
body.has-cfm-player { padding-bottom: 68px; }

    <h2>Cure Notices</h2>
    <p>What a cure notice is, when to issue one, what it needs to say, and why it should be your first move when contractor performance falls short.</p>
  </div>

  

  <div class="rfp-tabs" role="tablist">
    <button class="rfp-tab active" onclick="showRfpTab('learn', this)">📖 Learn</button>
    <button class="rfp-tab" onclick="showRfpTab('buildit', this)">🔨 Build It</button>

  </div>

  <!-- ═══════════════════════════ LEARN ═══════════════════════════ -->
  <div id="rfp-learn" class="rfp-panel active">

    <div class="learn-section">
      <h3><span class="section-num">1</span> What a Cure Notice Is</h3>
      <div class="learn-body">
        <p>A cure notice is a written notice from the contracting officer to the contractor stating that the government considers the contractor to be in danger of default for either <strong>failure to make progress</strong> or <strong>failure to perform</strong> the contract, and giving the contractor a specified period of time to cure the problem. It is governed by FAR 49.402-3(d) and (e).</p>
        <p>The cure notice is a prerequisite to termination for default in most situations. If you terminate a contractor for default without first issuing a cure notice (when one was required), the termination is likely to be converted to a termination for convenience on appeal, which means the contractor gets paid for work performed and you lose your leverage.</p>
        <p>A cure notice does not terminate anything. It does not modify the contract. It does not penalize the contractor. It tells the contractor: <strong>here is what is wrong, you have this many days to fix it, and if you do not fix it the government may terminate the contract for default.</strong> That is all it does. And that is why it should be your first step when you identify a performance problem.</p>
      </div>
    </div>

    <hr class="learn-divider">

    <div class="learn-section">
      <h3><span class="section-num">2</span> Skip the Letter of Concern</h3>
      <div class="learn-body">
        <p>Some offices have a practice of sending "letters of concern" or "letters of caution" before issuing a cure notice. These are not required by the FAR, have no legal effect, and create a problem: they add time between when you identify a deficiency and when you can act on it.</p>
        <p>Here is the practical issue. You notice the contractor is falling behind on deliveries. You send a letter of concern. The contractor responds with a recovery plan. The problem continues. You send another letter. Eventually the situation reaches a point where the contractor clearly cannot recover, and now you need to issue a cure notice followed by a show-cause letter and possibly a termination. All the time you spent on letters of concern did not advance the process by a single day.</p>
        <p>A cure notice, by contrast, starts the clock. It gives the contractor a defined period to fix the problem. If the problem gets fixed, everyone is better off. If it does not, you have a documented record that the contractor was put on notice, given a fair opportunity to cure, and failed to do so. That record is what protects the government if the termination is appealed.</p>

        <div class="highlight-box amber">
          <strong>A cure notice does not cause harm.</strong> It is not a punishment. It is not a black mark on the contractor's record. It is a formal statement of what is wrong and how long the contractor has to fix it. There is no reason to add an informal step before it. If the problem is worth documenting, it is worth a cure notice.
        </div>
      </div>
    </div>

    <hr class="learn-divider">

    <div class="learn-section">
      <h3><span class="section-num">3</span> When a Cure Notice Is Required</h3>
      <div class="learn-body">
        <p>FAR 49.402-3(d) requires a cure notice before termination for default when the contractor has failed to make progress or failed to perform any other provision of the contract (other than failure to deliver on time). The cure notice must give the contractor at least <strong>10 days</strong> to cure the failure.</p>

        <table class="rfp-table">
          <thead><tr><th>Situation</th><th>Cure Notice Required?</th></tr></thead>
          <tbody>
            <tr><td><strong>Contractor failing to make progress</strong> and endangering performance of the contract</td><td>Yes. FAR 49.402-3(d).</td></tr>
            <tr><td><strong>Contractor failing to perform</strong> a contract provision (other than delivery)</td><td>Yes. FAR 49.402-3(d).</td></tr>
            <tr><td><strong>Contractor failed to deliver</strong> by the contract delivery date (date has already passed)</td><td>Not required. You may proceed directly to a show-cause notice or termination. However, issuing a cure notice first is still good practice if there is any possibility the contractor can still deliver.</td></tr>
            <tr><td><strong>Contractor performance is substandard</strong> but the delivery date has not passed</td><td>Yes. This is a failure to make progress or perform.</td></tr>
          </tbody>
        </table>

        <p>The key distinction: if the delivery date has already passed, the FAR does not require a cure notice before termination for default. But if the contractor is struggling before the delivery date, you must issue a cure notice and give them a chance to fix it before you can terminate.</p>

        <div class="highlight-box tip">
          <strong>The 10-day minimum is a floor, not a target.</strong> Depending on the nature of the deficiency, you may need to give the contractor more than 10 days to realistically cure the problem. A cure period that is too short to allow actual correction may be viewed as a pretextual step toward a predetermined termination decision, which weakens your record.
        </div>
      </div>
    </div>

    <hr class="learn-divider">

    <div class="learn-section">
      <h3><span class="section-num">4</span> What Goes in the Cure Notice</h3>
      <div class="learn-body">
        <p>A cure notice must contain the following elements. If any of these are missing, the notice may be found deficient on appeal.</p>

        <ul style="color:var(--silver);line-height:1.9;font-size:0.92rem;padding-left:1.4rem;margin-bottom:1rem;">
          <li><strong>Identification of the contract:</strong> contract number, task order number if applicable, and contractor name.</li>
          <li><strong>Specific description of the failure:</strong> what the contractor is failing to do or failing to make progress on, referencing the specific contract provisions, PWS sections, or CLIN items involved. Do not be vague. "The contractor is not performing satisfactorily" is insufficient. "The contractor has failed to provide the required monthly status reports for October, November, and December 2025 as required by PWS Section 6.3" is specific.</li>
          <li><strong>Statement that the failure endangers performance:</strong> explain how the identified failure, if not corrected, endangers the contractor's ability to perform the contract.</li>
          <li><strong>The cure period:</strong> state the number of days the contractor has to cure the deficiency. Minimum 10 days per FAR 49.402-3(e). The cure period begins when the contractor receives the notice.</li>
          <li><strong>Statement of consequences:</strong> state that if the contractor fails to cure the deficiency within the specified period, the government may terminate the contract for default under FAR 52.249-8 (fixed-price) or FAR 52.249-9 (cost-reimbursement).</li>
        </ul>

        <div class="doc-block">
          <span class="doc-section-head">FAR 49.607(a) — Cure Notice Format</span>
          <div class="doc-body">
            <p>You are notified that the Government considers your [<em>specify the contractor's failure or failures</em>] a condition that is endangering performance of the contract. Therefore, unless this condition is cured within 10 days after receipt of this notice [<em>or insert any longer time that the Contracting Officer may consider reasonably necessary</em>], the Government may terminate for default under the terms and conditions of the [<em>insert clause title</em>] clause of this contract.</p>
          </div>
        </div>

        <p>That is the FAR-prescribed format. It is short. In practice, you should supplement this language with a specific description of the failure (dates, contract provisions, quantities) so the record is clear enough to support the next step if the contractor does not cure. The FAR format gives you the structure; your job is to fill in the bracket language with enough detail that anyone reading the record can understand exactly what the contractor was told to fix.</p>

        <div class="highlight-box warn">
          <strong>Coordinate with legal counsel.</strong> Termination actions, including the cure notice that may precede one, should be reviewed by your procurement attorney. The cure notice creates the record that supports or defeats a termination for default. Get it right the first time.
        </div>
      </div>
    </div>

    <hr class="learn-divider">

    <div class="learn-section">
      <h3><span class="section-num">5</span> After the Cure Period Expires</h3>
      <div class="learn-body">
        <p>When the cure period ends, one of three things has happened:</p>

        <p><strong>The contractor cured the deficiency.</strong> Document that the problem was resolved. The cure notice served its purpose. No further action is required unless the problem recurs.</p>

        <p><strong>The contractor partially cured or made meaningful progress.</strong> You have a judgment call. If the contractor is demonstrating good faith effort and making real progress, you may extend the cure period in writing. If the progress is cosmetic or insufficient, you may proceed to the next step. Document your reasoning either way.</p>

        <p><strong>The contractor failed to cure.</strong> At this point you have a documented record showing: (1) the contractor was notified of a specific deficiency, (2) the contractor was given a reasonable period to cure it, and (3) the contractor did not cure it. This record supports a termination for default. In most cases, the next step is a <strong>show-cause notice</strong> (covered in I-21), which gives the contractor one more opportunity to explain why the contract should not be terminated. After that, the termination decision is made, typically with significant involvement from your legal counsel and, in some agencies, a termination contracting officer (TCO).</p>

        <div class="integrity-box">
          <span class="integrity-label">Your Role vs. the TCO and Legal</span>
          Terminations for default are legally complex. The contractor can appeal to the boards of contract appeals (ASBCA, CBCA) or the Court of Federal Claims. The government bears the burden of proving the default was justified. Your job as the CO is to build the record: issue the cure notice correctly, document the deficiency with specificity, give a reasonable cure period, and document the outcome. Your legal counsel and, where applicable, your TCO handle the legal strategy and the termination decision itself. Do your part right and you give them what they need to protect the government's position.
        </div>
      </div>
    </div>

    <hr class="learn-divider">

    <div class="learn-section">
      <h3><span class="section-num">6</span> Common Mistakes</h3>
      <div class="learn-body">
        <p><strong>Vague descriptions of the deficiency.</strong> "The contractor's performance has been unsatisfactory" does not tell anyone what was wrong. Cite the specific PWS section, CLIN, or contract provision. Include dates, numbers, and objective facts. The cure notice needs to be specific enough that the contractor knows exactly what to fix and the record shows exactly what was at issue.</p>

        <p><strong>Cure period that is too short to allow actual correction.</strong> If the deficiency involves hiring staff, procuring materials, or restructuring a team, 10 days may not be realistic. A cure period that appears designed to fail looks pretextual on appeal. Give the contractor enough time to actually cure the problem.</p>

        <p><strong>Failing to send the notice in writing.</strong> Verbal warnings do not satisfy the FAR requirement. The cure notice must be in writing and you should confirm receipt (certified mail, email with read receipt, or hand delivery with signature).</p>

        <p><strong>Issuing the notice after the delivery date has already passed.</strong> If the delivery date passed and the contractor did not deliver, a cure notice is not required. You should issue a show-cause notice instead, or proceed to termination if the facts clearly support it. Issuing a cure notice in this situation is not wrong, but it adds time without legal benefit.</p>

        <p><strong>Not coordinating with legal.</strong> Cure notices create the record that may be litigated before a board of contract appeals. Your legal counsel should review the notice before you send it.</p>
      </div>
    </div>

  </div><!-- end learn panel -->

          + '<div class="buildit-card-title">' + sc.title + '</div>'
          + '<span class="buildit-card-badge">' + sc.badge + '</span>'
          + '</div>'
          + '<div class="buildit-card-desc">' + sc.desc + '</div>';

    html += '<div class="buildit-step">'
          + '<span class="buildit-step-label">' + sc.question + '</span>'
          + '<div class="buildit-options">';
    sc.options.forEach(function(o) {
      var sel = (buildAnswer === o.val) ? ' selected' : '';
      html += '<label class="buildit-option' + sel + '">'
            + '<input type="radio" name="action-' + sc.idx + '" value="' + o.val + '" onchange="selectAnswer(\'' + o.val + '\')"' + (buildAnswer === o.val ? ' checked' : '') + '>'
            + '<div><div class="buildit-option-title">' + o.title + '</div><div class="buildit-option-sub">' + o.sub + '</div></div>'
            + '</label>';
    });
    html += '</div></div>';

    html += '<div class="buildit-footer">'
          + '<button class="buildit-generate-btn" onclick="submitAnswer()">Submit</button>'
          + '<button class="buildit-reset-btn' + (buildGenerated ? ' shown' : '') + '" onclick="resetBuild()">Reset</button>'
          + '</div>';

    if (buildGenerated) {
      var fb = (sc.feedback && sc.feedback[buildAnswer]) ? sc.feedback[buildAnswer] : '<em>No feedback available.</em>';
      html += '<div class="buildit-result shown"><div style="padding:1rem 1.2rem;">'
            + '<span class="buildit-feedback-label">Assessment</span>'
            + '<div style="color:var(--silver);font-size:0.85rem;line-height:1.75;">' + fb + '</div>'
            + '</div></div>';
    }

    document.getElementById('buildit-mount').innerHTML = html;
  }

  function selectAnswer(val) {
    buildAnswer = val;
    if (buildGenerated) buildGenerated = false;
    renderBuildScenario();
  }

  function submitAnswer() {
    if (!buildAnswer) { alert('Select an action before submitting.'); return; }
    buildGenerated = true;
    renderBuildScenario();
  }

  function resetBuild() {
    buildAnswer = null;
    buildGenerated = false;
    renderBuildScenario();
  }

  if (document.readyState === 'loading') {
    document.addEventListener('DOMContentLoaded', renderBuildScenario);
  } else {
    renderBuildScenario();
  }
</script>

<!DOCTYPE html><html lang="en" style="--cfm-accent: #7c3aed;"><head>

  <meta charset="UTF-8">
  <meta name="viewport" content="width=device-width, initial-scale=1.0">
  <meta name="description" content="What a contracting officer actually does to evaluate contract labor standards: when SCLS applies, when Davis-Bacon applies, how to read a wage determination, the option-year price adjustment under 52.222-43, conformance requests, and the construction-side compliance duties that step up under FAR 22.406.">
  <title>Evaluating Contract Labor Standards | ContractingHQ</title>
  <link rel="preconnect" href="https://fonts.googleapis.com">
  <link rel="preconnect" href="https://fonts.gstatic.com" crossorigin="">
  <link href="https://fonts.googleapis.com/css2?family=Inter:wght@300;400;500;600;700;800&family=Rajdhani:wght@500;600;700&display=swap" rel="stylesheet">
  <link rel="stylesheet" href="styles.css">
  <link rel="icon" type="image/svg+xml" href="data:image/svg+xml,%3Csvg%20xmlns%3D%27http%3A%2F%2Fwww.w3.org%2F2000%2Fsvg%27%20viewBox%3D%270%200%2032%2032%27%3E%3Cpath%20d%3D%27M16%202%20L28%207%20L28%2018%20C28%2024%2022%2029%2016%2031%20C10%2029%204%2024%204%2018%20L4%207%20Z%27%20fill%3D%27%230d1117%27%20stroke%3D%27%234a9eff%27%20stroke-width%3D%271.5%27%2F%3E%3Ctext%20x%3D%2716%27%20y%3D%2721%27%20text-anchor%3D%27middle%27%20font-family%3D%27Arial%2Csans-serif%27%20font-weight%3D%27bold%27%20font-size%3D%279%27%20fill%3D%27%234a9eff%27%20letter-spacing%3D%270.5%27%3EKTHQ%3C%2Ftext%3E%3C%2Fsvg%3E">
  <style>.bmc-btn{display:inline-flex;align-items:center;gap:.4rem;background:#FFDD00;color:#000;border-radius:8px;padding:.45rem 1rem;font-weight:700;font-size:.83rem;text-decoration:none;transition:opacity .2s,transform .15s}.bmc-btn:hover{opacity:.88;transform:translateY(-1px)}</style>
  <style>
    .rfp-bg {
      background:
        radial-gradient(ellipse 110% 35% at 50% 0%,   rgba(251,191,36,0.09) 0%, transparent 65%),
        radial-gradient(ellipse 80%  25% at 0%   50%,  rgba(251,191,36,0.05) 0%, transparent 55%),
        radial-gradient(ellipse 80%  25% at 100% 50%,  rgba(251,191,36,0.05) 0%, transparent 55%),
        radial-gradient(ellipse 110% 30% at 50% 100%,  rgba(251,191,36,0.07) 0%, transparent 65%),
        #040d1f;
      padding: 0 0 6rem;
      min-height: 100vh;
    }
    .rfp-intro { text-align: center; padding: 2.5rem 1.5rem 0; }
    .rfp-intro-tag { display: inline-block; background: rgba(251,191,36,0.1); border: 1px solid rgba(251,191,36,0.3); color: #fbbf24; font-size: 0.68rem; font-weight: 700; letter-spacing: 2px; text-transform: uppercase; padding: 0.25rem 0.9rem; border-radius: 100px; margin-bottom: 0.65rem; }
    .rfp-intro h2 { font-family: 'Rajdhani', sans-serif; font-size: clamp(1.4rem,3vw,2rem); font-weight: 700; color: var(--white); margin-bottom: 0.4rem; }
    .rfp-intro p { color: var(--silver); font-size: 0.9rem; max-width: 680px; margin: 0 auto 1.5rem; line-height: 1.6; }

    .rfp-tabs { display: flex; gap: 0; border-bottom: 1px solid rgba(251,191,36,0.15); background: rgba(4,13,31,0.95); position: sticky; top: 0; z-index: 90; backdrop-filter: blur(8px); flex-wrap: wrap; }
    .rfp-tab { padding: 0.85rem 1.5rem; font-size: 0.85rem; font-weight: 700; text-transform: uppercase; letter-spacing: 1px; color: var(--silver); background: none; border: none; border-bottom: 3px solid transparent; cursor: pointer; transition: all 0.18s; font-family: inherit; white-space: nowrap; }
    .rfp-tab:hover { color: var(--white); }
    .rfp-tab.active { color: #fbbf24; border-bottom-color: #fbbf24; }
    .rfp-panel { display: none; padding: 3rem 1.5rem; max-width: 920px; margin: 0 auto; }
    .rfp-panel.active { display: block; }

    .learn-section { margin-bottom: 2.5rem; }
    .learn-section h3 { font-family: 'Rajdhani', sans-serif; font-size: 1.35rem; font-weight: 700; color: var(--white); margin-bottom: 0.75rem; display: flex; align-items: center; gap: 0.5rem; }
    .learn-section h3 .section-num { display: inline-flex; align-items: center; justify-content: center; width: 30px; height: 30px; border-radius: 8px; background: rgba(251,191,36,0.12); color: #fbbf24; font-size: 0.85rem; font-weight: 700; flex-shrink: 0; }
    .learn-body { color: var(--silver); font-size: 0.92rem; line-height: 1.75; }
    .learn-body p { margin-bottom: 1rem; }
    .learn-body strong { color: var(--white); font-weight: 600; }
    .learn-body ul { margin: 0.5rem 0 1rem 1.3rem; padding: 0; }
    .learn-body ul li { margin-bottom: 0.4rem; }
    .learn-body ol { margin: 0.5rem 0 1rem 1.3rem; padding: 0; }
    .learn-body ol li { margin-bottom: 0.4rem; }
    .learn-divider { border: none; border-top: 1px solid rgba(251,191,36,0.08); margin: 2rem 0; }

    .highlight-box { background: rgba(74,158,255,0.05); border: 1px solid rgba(74,158,255,0.15); border-radius: 12px; padding: 1rem 1.25rem; margin: 1rem 0; font-size: 0.88rem; color: var(--silver); }
    .highlight-box strong { color: var(--white); }
    .highlight-box.warn { background: rgba(248,113,113,0.05); border-color: rgba(248,113,113,0.2); }
    .highlight-box.warn strong { color: #fca5a5; }
    .highlight-box.tip { background: rgba(52,211,153,0.05); border-color: rgba(52,211,153,0.2); }
    .highlight-box.tip strong { color: #6ee7b7; }
    .highlight-box.amber { background: rgba(251,191,36,0.06); border-color: rgba(251,191,36,0.22); }
    .highlight-box.amber strong { color: #fcd34d; }

    .rfp-table { width: 100%; border-collapse: collapse; font-size: 0.82rem; margin: 1rem 0; }
    .rfp-table th { background: rgba(251,191,36,0.1); color: #fbbf24; font-weight: 700; text-align: left; padding: 0.6rem 0.85rem; border-bottom: 1px solid rgba(251,191,36,0.2); font-size: 0.72rem; text-transform: uppercase; letter-spacing: 0.5px; }
    .rfp-table td { color: var(--silver); padding: 0.6rem 0.85rem; border-bottom: 1px solid rgba(74,158,255,0.06); vertical-align: top; }
    .rfp-table tr:hover td { background: rgba(251,191,36,0.03); }
    .rfp-table td strong { color: var(--white); }
    .rfp-table tr.total-row td { background: rgba(251,191,36,0.08); color: var(--white); font-weight: 700; border-top: 1px solid rgba(251,191,36,0.25); }
    .rfp-table td.num { text-align: right; font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums; }
    .rfp-table th.num { text-align: right; }

    .flag-cell { display: inline-block; font-size: 0.68rem; font-weight: 700; padding: 0.12rem 0.5rem; border-radius: 100px; letter-spacing: 0.5px; text-transform: uppercase; }
    .flag-cell.ok { color: #6ee7b7; background: rgba(52,211,153,0.1); border: 1px solid rgba(52,211,153,0.25); }
    .flag-cell.warn { color: #fcd34d; background: rgba(251,191,36,0.1); border: 1px solid rgba(251,191,36,0.3); }
    .flag-cell.bad { color: #fca5a5; background: rgba(248,113,113,0.1); border: 1px solid rgba(248,113,113,0.35); }

    /* Scenario sheet */
    .showme-part-label { display: inline-block; font-size: 0.62rem; font-weight: 700; letter-spacing: 2px; text-transform: uppercase; color: #fbbf24; background: rgba(251,191,36,0.08); border: 1px solid rgba(251,191,36,0.22); border-radius: 100px; padding: 0.22rem 0.8rem; margin-bottom: 0.5rem; }
    .scenario-sheet { background: rgba(4,10,26,0.8); border: 1px solid rgba(74,158,255,0.2); border-radius: 14px; overflow: hidden; margin: 1.2rem 0 1.6rem; box-shadow: 0 6px 22px rgba(0,0,0,0.35); }
    .scenario-head { background: linear-gradient(180deg, rgba(251,191,36,0.14) 0%, rgba(251,191,36,0.05) 100%); border-bottom: 1px solid rgba(251,191,36,0.25); padding: 1rem 1.3rem; }
    .scenario-head .scn-label { display: block; font-size: 0.62rem; font-weight: 700; text-transform: uppercase; letter-spacing: 2px; color: #fbbf24; margin-bottom: 0.25rem; }

  <div class="rfp-intro">
    <div class="rfp-intro-tag">Topic I-18 • Labor Standards & Services</div>
    <h2>Evaluating Contract Labor Standards</h2>
    <p>What a contracting officer actually does to keep a services or construction contract aligned with federal labor standards. Two lanes with different rules: SCLS for services (where DOL does most of the enforcement), and Davis-Bacon for construction (where the agency has real compliance duties). The administrative work at solicitation and option exercise, the weekly payroll review that steps up on DBA, and what happens when DOL shows up.</p>
  </div>

  

  <div class="rfp-tabs" role="tablist">
    <button class="rfp-tab active" onclick="showTab('learn', this)">📖 Learn</button>
    <button class="rfp-tab" onclick="showTab('showme', this)">🔍 Show Me</button>
  </div>

  <!-- LEARN -->
  <div id="tab-learn" class="rfp-panel active">

    <div class="learn-section">
      <h3><span class="section-num">1</span> What "Evaluating Labor Standards" Actually Means for a CO</h3>
      <div class="learn-body">
        <p>The phrase "evaluating contract labor standards" can sound like the CO is auditing contractor payrolls. For a services CO running SCLS-covered contracts, that framing is misleading. DOL's Wage and Hour Division has primary enforcement authority. The CO's job is to get the setup right at solicitation, handle the option-year price adjustments, process conformance requests when they come up, and cooperate with DOL when a complaint or investigation arrives.</p>

        <p>The agency's role steps up considerably on construction. FAR 22.406 gives the contracting agency compliance duties on Davis-Bacon work that do not exist for SCLS: reviewing weekly certified payrolls, conducting employee interviews, investigating apparent violations before they route to DOL. A CO who splits their time between services and construction will feel the difference.</p>

        <div class="highlight-box amber">
          <strong>Two lanes, different rules.</strong> On services contracts under SCLS, the CO's role is mostly administrative (WD management, price adjustments, conformance requests), and DOL handles enforcement. On construction contracts under DBA, the CO has active compliance monitoring duties written into FAR 22.406 including weekly payroll review. A CO who walks onto a construction job expecting the SCLS lane will miss things that are specifically the agency's responsibility.
        </div>
      </div>
    </div>

    <hr class="learn-divider">

    <div class="learn-section">
      <h3><span class="section-num">2</span> When SCLS Applies, When DBA Applies, When Neither Does</h3>
      <div class="learn-body">
        <p>The starting question on any contract is which labor standards law applies, and the answer comes from the principal purpose test, not from whether some labor shows up in the work.</p>

        <table class="rfp-table">
          <thead>
            <tr>
              <th>Test</th>
              <th>SCLS<br>(Service Contract Labor Standards)</th>
              <th>DBA<br>(Davis-Bacon Act)</th>
            </tr>
          </thead>
          <tbody>
            <tr>
              <td><strong>Principal purpose</strong></td>
              <td>Furnishing services through the use of service employees.</td>
              <td>Construction, alteration, or repair (including painting and decorating) of public buildings or public works.</td>
            </tr>
            <tr>
              <td><strong>Threshold</strong></td>
              <td>Over $2,500.</td>
              <td>Over $2,000.</td>
            </tr>
            <tr>
              <td><strong>Wage determination source</strong></td>
              <td>DOL service contract wage determinations via sam.gov/wage-determinations.</td>
              <td>DOL Davis-Bacon wage determinations via sam.gov/wage-determinations, by construction type.</td>
            </tr>
            <tr>
              <td><strong>Core FAR clauses</strong></td>
              <td>52.222-41 (SCLS), 52.222-42 (statement of equivalent rates for federal hires), 52.222-43 (price adjustment, multiple year and option).</td>
              <td>52.222-6 (Construction Wage Rate Requirements), 52.222-8 (payrolls and basic records), 52.222-10 (compliance), 52.222-11 (subcontracts).</td>
            </tr>
          </tbody>
        </table>

        <p>Common exemptions worth knowing:</p>
        <ul>
          <li><strong>Bona fide executive, administrative, and professional employees</strong> under 29 CFR Part 541 are exempt from both SCLS and DBA rate requirements.</li>
          <li><strong>Certain maintenance, calibration, or repair of specific equipment</strong> may be exempt from SCLS under 41 U.S.C. 6703 when the narrow statutory tests are met.</li>
          <li><strong>Supply contracts</strong> fall under the Walsh-Healey Public Contracts Act, not SCLS or DBA. A contract whose principal purpose is to furnish supplies is not an SCLS contract even if there is incidental labor in the delivery.</li>
          <li><strong>Contracts for professional services</strong> (architects, engineers, attorneys, consultants) are typically outside SCLS because the workforce is exempt under Part 541.</li>
        </ul>

        <p>Mixed-purpose contracts come up. A services contract that includes a small amount of construction, or a construction contract that includes follow-on maintenance, can trigger both sets of requirements for the respective portions. FAR 22.402(b) walks the treatment.</p>

        <div class="highlight-box tip">
          <strong>Principal purpose is the right question.</strong> Almost every contract involves some labor of some kind. The question is what activity the contract exists to accomplish. A custodial contract is SCLS. A roof replacement is DBA. A grounds maintenance contract with a one-time sidewalk repair is SCLS for the ongoing grounds work and DBA for the sidewalk portion, with the clauses flowing to the relevant work.
        </div>
      </div>
    </div>

    <hr class="learn-divider">

    <div class="learn-section">
      <h3><span class="section-num">3</span> Reading a Wage Determination</h3>
      <div class="learn-body">
        <p>A wage determination (WD) is a DOL-issued document that sets the minimum hourly rate and fringe benefits the contractor must pay each category of worker on the contract. Reading one takes about five minutes once you know the structure.</p>

        <p><strong>SCLS wage determinations</strong> (the "Register of Wage Determinations Under The Service Contract Act") include:</p>
        <ul>
          <li><strong>WD number and revision.</strong> Example: WD 2015-5395, Revision 24. The revision number changes as DOL updates the rates, usually annually.</li>
          <li><strong>Geographic coverage.</strong> Counties, state, or specific installations.</li>
          <li><strong>Effective date.</strong> When the revision takes effect for application purposes.</li>
          <li><strong>Directory of occupations.</strong> SCA Directory codes and titles (Janitor 11150, Landscape Specialist 23580, Tractor Operator 23860, and so on).</li>
          <li><strong>Minimum hourly rate by occupation.</strong></li>
          <li><strong>Health and Welfare (H&W) fringe rate.</strong> Usually a single hourly rate applied across most occupations.</li>
          <li><strong>Vacation and holiday schedule.</strong></li>
          <li><strong>Executive Order minimum wage</strong> where applicable. Check the current status of any applicable EO floor, since this has changed with administration.</li>
        </ul>

        <p><strong>DBA wage determinations</strong> look different. They are organized by construction type (Building, Heavy, Highway, Residential), list craft rates (Carpenter, Electrician, Laborer, Roofer, etc.), and show fringe benefits as a separate hourly dollar amount rather than a single H&W rate. A DBA WD often references union agreements as the source of the rate and may include separate rates for apprentices and helpers.</p>

        <div class="highlight-box">
          <strong>The "occupations not listed" problem.</strong> If the contract requires labor in a category that does not appear on the attached WD, the contractor cannot simply pick a rate and pay it. A conformance process is required before the work is performed. Section 6 walks the mechanics.
        </div>
      </div>
    </div>

    <hr class="learn-divider">

    <div class="learn-section">
      <h3><span class="section-num">4</span> Getting the Right WD Into the Solicitation</h3>
      <div class="learn-body">
        <p>Wage determinations live on sam.gov/wage-determinations. The workflow is short and the same basic shape for both SCLS and DBA:</p>

        <ol>
          <li><strong>Identify the type.</strong> SCLS for a services contract, DBA for a construction contract, picked from the principal purpose test.</li>
          <li><strong>Identify the performance location.</strong> County, state, or specific installation. Multi-location contracts need WDs for each location.</li>
          <li><strong>Pull the current WD.</strong> For SCLS, the Register of Wage Determinations for that county. For DBA, the construction type (Building, Heavy, etc.) that matches the work.</li>
          <li><strong>Attach the WD to the solicitation.</strong> Incorporated by reference with the number, revision, and effective date captured in the contract record.</li>
          <li><strong>File the WD baseline.</strong> Keep a copy in the contract file so that the option-year price adjustment calculation has a clean starting point.</li>
        </ol>

        <p>For SCLS solicitations where the standard WD selector does not match the actual work (unusual location, non-standard occupation mix), DOL provides an <strong>e98 process</strong>. The CO submits an e98 request through DOL and receives a project-specific wage determination. This is uncommon on routine services contracts.</p>

        <p>Effective date rules are specific and worth getting right. The WD in effect at the time of solicitation issuance is the one that typically attaches, with timing exceptions for solicitations held open past certain dates and for option exercises. FAR 22.1008 (SCLS) and FAR 22.404 (DBA) walk the timing in detail.</p>

        <div class="highlight-box warn">
          <strong>Check the revision on the day you issue.</strong> Attaching an outdated WD is a common solicitation error. The revision number on your draft copy from three weeks ago is probably not the one that should be in the issued solicitation. DOL revises WDs regularly. Pull the current version from SAM.gov on the day you issue and confirm the revision number that lands in the file matches.
        </div>
      </div>
    </div>

    <hr class="learn-divider">

    <div class="learn-section">
      <h3><span class="section-num">5</span> The Option Year Price Adjustment (SCLS)</h3>
      <div class="learn-body">
        <p>This is where most services COs spend the bulk of their labor standards time, and it is the section worth reading carefully.</p>

        <p>FAR 52.222-43 (Fair Labor Standards Act and Service Contract Labor Standards, Price Adjustment, Multiple Year and Option Contracts) requires a contract price adjustment at each option exercise to reflect the cost impact of a revised wage determination. The clause is mandatory on most multi-year and option-year SCLS contracts. FAR 52.222-44 handles the comparable situation for certain multiple-year contracts without options.</p>

        <p>The mechanics:</p>

        <ol>
          <li><strong>Pull the current WD before the option exercise.</strong> Grab the SCLS WD for the performance location from SAM.gov. If the revision is newer than the one currently incorporated in the contract, the clause is triggered.</li>
          <li><strong>Notify the contractor and incorporate the revised WD.</strong> By bilateral or unilateral modification, depending on how the office prefers to handle it. The contract now references the new revision.</li>
          <li><strong>The contractor has 30 days to submit actual cost impact.</strong> The clause limits recovery to the actual labor cost delta: new hourly rate minus old hourly rate, applied to actual hours in each affected category. H&W delta works the same way.</li>
          <li><strong>The CO reviews the submission.</strong> Mathematical accuracy, consistency with the labor categories actually used on the contract, no claimed hours for categories that are not performing, no G&A or profit applied on top of the wage delta.</li>
          <li><strong>Modify and document.</strong> Bilateral modification adjusts the option-year ceiling price. File the modification, the contractor's submission, and the new WD in the contract file.</li>
        </ol>

        <p>The adjustment should be in place before the option period begins. A CO who discovers at month six of an option that the revised WD was never incorporated has a messier situation. The clause still requires the adjustment, but the contractor has already been performing at the new rates and the reconciliation is harder than a clean 30-day submission would have been.</p>

        <div class="highlight-box amber">
          <strong>Actual cost impact only.</strong> 52.222-43 is a vehicle for the labor rate delta and nothing more. A contractor submission that includes G&A on top of the wage delta, a profit markup on the increase, or hours for categories that are not actually performing should be pushed back on. The clause language is specific: "the actual increase or decrease in wages and fringe benefits as a result of the adjustment in wages and fringe benefits required to conform with the new wage determination."
        </div>
      </div>
    </div>

    <hr class="learn-divider">

    <div class="learn-section">
      <h3><span class="section-num">6</span> Conformance Requests</h3>
      <div class="learn-body">
        <p>When the contract requires a labor category that is not on the attached SCLS wage determination, the contractor cannot simply pick a rate. FAR 52.222-41(c) and DOL's conformance process at 29 CFR 4.6(b)(2) require the contractor to submit a <strong>conformance request using SF 1444</strong> ("Request For Authorization of Additional Classification and Rate").</p>

        <p>The process in practical terms:</p>

        <ol>
          <li><strong>Contractor identifies the gap.</strong> A labor category not listed on the WD is needed for the work.</li>
          <li><strong>Contractor proposes a rate and fringe</strong> that bear a reasonable relationship to other listed categories on the same WD.</li>
          <li><strong>Contractor submits SF 1444 through the CO.</strong></li>
          <li><strong>CO reviews.</strong> Does the proposed rate sit in a sensible place relative to similar categories already on the WD? Is the classification well-defined? The CO then forwards the request to DOL's Wage and Hour Division.</li>
          <li><strong>DOL reviews and responds.</strong> Approve, modify, or deny. Typical turnaround is weeks to months.</li>
          <li><strong>Approved rate is retroactive</strong> to the first day the unlisted work was performed.</li>
        </ol>

        <p>A practical observation: many contracting offices do not actively process conformance requests. The paperwork burden is real, DOL's turnaround is slow, and the volume a single CO might see in a year is low. Offices with a dedicated labor advisor or an office lead who handles conformances usually have the CO flag the need and route to that person. Offices without that support handle it directly when they have to, or (more often) the gap gets managed through a better-scoped next solicitation.</p>

        <div class="highlight-box">
          <strong>Routing note.</strong> If your office has someone who handles conformances, route them there. If not, and conformance needs are showing up on the same contract repeatedly, the longer-term fix is usually in how the next solicitation is scoped and which labor categories are requested on the initial WD. Avoiding conformances through better scoping is usually a better investment than processing them one by one.
        </div>
      </div>
    </div>

    <hr class="learn-divider">

    <div class="learn-section">
      <h3><span class="section-num">7</span> The Construction Lane Is Different</h3>
      <div class="learn-body">
        <p>Davis-Bacon contracts give the contracting agency compliance duties that SCLS contracts do not. A CO picking up a construction contract needs to know what steps up.</p>

        <p><strong>Weekly certified payrolls.</strong> FAR 22.406-6 requires the contractor to submit a weekly certified payroll (Form WH-347 or equivalent) covering every employee performing work on the site of the work. Each payroll is certified by the contractor as accurate and compliant with the wage determination. The contracting agency reviews these as they come in, not just at the end of the contract.</p>

        <p>What the payroll review is actually looking for:</p>
        <ul>
          <li>Every employee has a classification that matches one on the WD, or has a conformance in place.</li>
          <li>The hourly rate paid meets or exceeds the WD rate for that classification.</li>
          <li>Fringe benefits are being paid, either in cash or into a bona fide plan, at the rate on the WD.</li>
          <li>Overtime premiums are calculated correctly on the basic rate.</li>
          <li>Apprentices are registered with a bona fide DOL-recognized apprenticeship program, and the apprentice-to-journeyman ratio on the job is within the program's allowed ratio. A worker paid at apprentice rates without proper registration must be paid the journey rate as the remedy under FAR 22.406-4.</li>
          <li>The hours reported are consistent with what is being observed on the job site, to the extent the CO or a representative conducts site visits.</li>
        </ul>

        <p><strong>Employee interviews.</strong> FAR 22.406-6(b) authorizes on-site interviews with contractor employees using <strong>SF 1445</strong> ("Labor Standards Interview"). These are short conversations, not depositions. The interviewer confirms the employee's name, classification, rate, and hours against the payroll submission. Discrepancies between the interview and the payroll are a significant finding.</p>

        <p><strong>Site postings.</strong> The contractor must post <strong>WH-1321</strong> ("Notice to Employees Working on Federal or Federally Financed Construction Projects") and the applicable wage determination at the site of the work in a location accessible to the employees.</p>

        <p><strong>Investigations of apparent violations.</strong> When payroll review or interviews surface an apparent violation, FAR 22.406-8 walks the agency's investigation process. The agency has the first look. Matters not resolved at the agency level route to DOL.</p>

        <div class="highlight-box warn">
          <strong>The DBA agency duties are real and are in the FAR.</strong> A CO who treats a construction contract like a services contract and skips the weekly payroll review is missing a requirement that sits specifically on the agency, not on DOL. If the office does not have bandwidth for weekly payroll review across construction contracts, that is a staffing conversation to have with leadership, not a reason to skip the requirement.
        </div>
      </div>
    </div>

    <hr class="learn-divider">

    <div class="learn-section">
      <h3><span class="section-num">8</span> When DOL Shows Up</h3>
      <div class="learn-body">
        <p>Both SCLS and DBA complaints route to DOL's Wage and Hour Division for investigation. A CO managing a contract under DOL investigation has a specific role and a specific set of things to stay out of.</p>

        <p>What typically happens:</p>

        <ul>
          <li>A complaint originates from an employee, a union, or (less often) an anonymous tip.</li>
          <li>WHD opens an investigation and may request contract documents, wage determinations, payrolls, and contact with the CO.</li>
          <li>The CO's role is to cooperate, provide requested documentation, and let DOL lead the investigation. The CO does not separately adjudicate the labor claim.</li>
          <li>The contract continues. An open DOL investigation by itself is not a basis to stop work, withhold payment, or terminate the contract. Withholding of contract funds for back wages is a DOL-initiated action with specific procedures under 29 CFR Part 5 (DBA) or 29 CFR Part 4 (SCLS).</li>
          <li>Outcomes can include back wage computations, civil money penalties, and in serious or repeated cases, debarment from future federal contracts under 41 U.S.C. 6706 (SCLS) or 29 CFR 5.12 (DBA).</li>
        </ul>

        <p>The CO stays in coordination with DOL throughout but does not run a parallel investigation. If DOL computes back wages, the CO's role is to process the withholding or payment adjustment DOL directs, on the timeline DOL directs.</p>

        <div class="highlight-box tip">
          <strong>Two things to have ready.</strong> If a DOL investigation opens on a contract you manage, the two fastest things to pull are the solicitation with the attached WD (and all subsequent revisions incorporated by modification), and the contractor's certified payrolls (DBA) or personnel records the contractor has provided. DOL will ask for both early. Having them organized saves days of back-and-forth.
        </div>
      </div>
    </div>

    <hr class="learn-divider">

    <div class="learn-section">
      <h3><span class="section-num">9</span> A Realistic CO Checklist</h3>
      <div class="learn-body">
        <p>The CO's labor standards touchpoints across a contract's life, split by lane:</p>

        <table class="rfp-table">
          <thead>
            <tr>
              <th>Touchpoint</th>
              <th>SCLS services contract</th>
              <th>DBA construction contract</th>
            </tr>
          </thead>
          <tbody>
            <tr>
              <td><strong>Pre-solicitation</strong></td>
              <td>Confirm SCLS applies (principal purpose, threshold, exemptions). Pull the current SCLS WD from SAM.gov for the performance location.</td>
              <td>Confirm DBA applies (construction, $2,000 threshold). Pull the current DBA WD for the construction type and location.</td>
            </tr>
            <tr>
              <td><strong>Solicitation</strong></td>
              <td>Attach the WD. Confirm the revision on the issue date. Flow 52.222-41, 52.222-42, 52.222-43.</td>
              <td>Attach the WD. Flow 52.222-6, 52.222-8, 52.222-10, 52.222-11 and the DBA-related reps and certs.</td>
            </tr>
            <tr>
              <td><strong>Award</strong></td>
              <td>Incorporate the WD by reference. File the baseline WD version for future price adjustments.</td>
              <td>Incorporate the WD. Brief the contractor on weekly WH-347 submission requirements and posting obligations.</td>
            </tr>
            <tr>
              <td><strong>During performance</strong></td>
              <td>Route conformance requests to the labor advisor or process SF 1444 if handled directly. Cooperate with any DOL inquiry that opens.</td>
              <td>Review weekly WH-347 payrolls. Conduct occasional SF 1445 employee interviews. Verify WH-1321 and WD postings on site visits. Investigate apparent violations per FAR 22.406-8.</td>
            </tr>
            <tr>
              <td><strong>Option exercise</strong></td>
              <td>Pull current WD from SAM.gov. If revised, incorporate and process the 52.222-43 price adjustment before the option period begins.</td>
              <td>Pull current WD. Incorporate per the contract's DBA option-year terms, which vary by contract type and clause set.</td>
            </tr>
            <tr>
              <td><strong>Closeout</strong></td>
              <td>Confirm no open conformance or DOL issues. File the final WD version with the closeout record.</td>
              <td>Confirm no open payroll disputes, no open DOL investigation, and that final certified payrolls are on file.</td>
            </tr>
          </tbody>
        </table>

        <div class="highlight-box">
          <strong>The rhythm differs by lane.</strong> Most of the services-side work is concentrated at solicitation, award, and option exercise. The middle of performance is quiet unless a conformance or a complaint comes up. Most of the construction-side work is concentrated during performance, because weekly payroll review is an ongoing obligation. A CO managing both lanes benefits from recognizing the rhythm and planning workload accordingly.
        </div>
      </div>
    </div>

  </div><!-- end learn panel -->

      <h3><span class="section-num">🔍</span> Two Scenarios, Side by Side</h3>

Scenario B is one week of DBA payroll review on a small roof replacement contract at the same base. Both are executed by Capt. J. Holloway, 56 CONS.</p>
